canonical_check.why: The handoff (3 Sep) records the film corpora as 77 BUU files, 0 CSXA images and IEEE, AASCE and BUU behind forms; the manifest (8 Oct) records the same corpora on disk at full size (CSXA 4,963 films; BUU 3,600 patients, 7,200 films; NHANES 17,073 and 543; VinDr 10,466; AASCE 609; Mendeley 714; IEEE 236; Spinal-AI 20,000), and the any-view plan says in its own words that the 3 Sep handoff had 77 BUU files while it reports BUU as held with 3,600 people. The manifest does not cite the handoff and does not carry its rules (the 208 Honduran films as the only cross-site test set, IEEE never for training, patient-disjoint splits, VinDr as restricted rather than credentialed), and the registry later excludes Mendeley outright, so the later page supersedes the holdings but not the lineage decisions; those survive only on the handoff, the board and the decisions page.

clusters.unsourced_summary: The September pages (the X-ray handoff and the vertebra-detector field report) assert that CSXA is the largest annotated lateral set in existence, that CM Spine is the only public intraoperative source, and that Google Drive caps folder downloads at about 50 files, none with a survey or a citation; the board and the decisions page, which copy each other, assert that no published work uses DRRs to supply level identity to a 2D model, that the published state of the art on radiographs is AUC 0.84 at 62.3 % prevalence without naming the study, and that 4.0 % is the population LSTV rate, which the protocol draft puts at 15.3 % and research directions at 9 to 18 %. The 8 October trio (the handoff, the literature-state and research directions) share the statements that every planning value assumed 95 to 99 % with no measurement behind it, that 97.6 % cannot be exceeded at any reachable n, and that no radiologist has read any acquired CT, with the power figures 35, 22 and 19 and the accuracy pair 97.4 % and 74.8 % repeated without run ids or the calculation. The manifest, the registry and the FluoroCap card repeat that no patient was imaged for FluoroCap as the ethics basis with no determination cited. The atlas calls SX-Stitch the only published collection of overlapping intraoperative C-arm frames while the registry calls the Bern runs the only overlapping travelling frames found and the C-ArmLSpine sweeps the only confirmed consecutive sequences with a paired volume. Research directions states that Castellvi type I is 68 % of all LSTV with no reference. Licence statements for BUU (an EULA forbidding redistribution, on the manifest and research directions) stand beside the registry's own line that the licence is unread by the owner.
clusters.stale_summary: Every primary page is dated and overtaken: the X-ray handoff's grid state was verified 3 September 2026 (77 BUU files, no CSXA, IEEE behind a subscription, PhysioNet DUA 1.5.0, CSXA V3.0); the manifest is as of 7 October with batch B00 cut over and its finalize pending, B13 awaiting the owner's decision, the home walk still running, live routes untested and six licence conflicts (CTPelvic1K, VerSe, DeepFluoro, Geneva hip, Ljubljana, SpineSAC) marked unknown; the literature-state of 8 October says it is being cross-referenced and that no drafted request is recorded as sent; the atlas is as of 17 October with every request line reading Sent: not recorded and the Radiopaedia fee unconfirmed that day; the registry was rendered 20 October with its sample-level counts empty until a grid job runs, case39 with no export yet, LUMOS never fetched, RSNA 2022 never unpacked, ten VerSe series never downloaded, BUU's licence unread, VinDr's own determination pending, Balgrist and SX-Stitch requests drafted and never sent, and no gated CT agreement signed. The grid pipeline of 21 October then records 26 requests sent and 5 granted, a signed and paid Radiopaedia licence awaiting countersignature, VinDr-PCXR access granted on 21 October, an RSNA RATIC download link that expires 2026-10-28 02:38 UTC, 15 recipes still marked to confirm, no shard built and no job run, on a schedule running 23 October to 2 November with the provisional filing on 30 October and the CNS talk on 2 November. The secondary pages carry their own dates: the FluoroCap card's manifest was generated 2026-09-14 with reader labels pending and version 0.3 in progress; the board is dated 11 September with IRB files still public (the decisions page records the purge done); the lab recipe says the public mirror is still v10 on 2026-09-27; the 8 October handoff says the provisional filing is not recorded and the migration in progress; research directions says nothing ran on the grid and 33 were graded today; the any-view plan says the census job goes to the grid next and the IPCAI 2025 set is not yet held; the retrospective protocol is Date Submitted: Draft with an AIDaS deadline of 16 October 2026 already past and a target of January 2027; the eProtocol draft is dated 15 September with its 40,000-study cohort unconfirmed; and the COBRA embargoed cases are released on 2032-03-01.
clusters.notes: The plain-text extracts of the registry and the atlas truncate their embedded arrays after the first entry, so the registry's 60 records were read from the page's own JSON (const DATA in /home/user/SchwingNet/artifacts/schwingnet-data-registry/index.html) and the atlas's 217 entries from window.ATLAS in /home/user/SchwingNet/artifacts/fluoroscopy-data-atlas/index.html, extracted with a script run under python3 -I into /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/1b2f17bd-1fd4-5865-b98a-4797cc8ea3ad/scratchpad/helper/cluster_ds/registry.json and atlas.json; the quoted registry and atlas lines were verified there, the other artifacts' quotes come from their inventory records. The atlas entries confirmed the 150 Elekta exports, the SX-Stitch 'only published collection' line, DysphagiaBank at 87 files and 19 GB held, SpineSAC at 5,492 files with five or six C-arms, and the Bournemouth lumbar set as the only confirmed lumbar cine (a request source, so not in conflict with the atlas's 'found nowhere public' for lateral lumbar flexion-extension). Secondary pages dated 11 to 27 September (the board, decisions, lab recipe, field report, X-ray handoff, FluoroCap card, protocol drafts) are earlier than every primary page and most of their disagreements with the October pages are superseded holdings rather than live contradictions; they are listed where the later page does not say it replaces them. clusters.cluster: FluoroCap: the corpus, its pipeline and its audits

candidates.topic: Figure-mate region agreement with constraint decoding versus the level model alone (same corpus, same date, 2026-09-14)
candidates.statement_a: The card's evaluation table gives 88% figure-mate region agreement for the decoder and 52% for the model alone, with no pair count.
candidates.quote_a: figure mates agreeing on region (decoder) | 88% | panels of the same figure with the same caption levels; 52% for the model alone (partly induced by the shared caption)
candidates.statement_b: The audit of the same day gives 91.5% for the decoder on 519 pairs and 52.1% for the model alone on 468 pairs.
candidates.quote_b: Constraint decoding lifts caption-free region agreement from 52.1% to 91.5% ... 519 pairs for the decoder, 468 for the model run alone.
candidates.why_it_matters: The decoder's headline number is either 88% or 91.5% for the same quantity on the same date; a planner citing one page misquotes the other, and only the audit says how many pairs were counted.

candidates.topic: What the panels without a vertebra box are: detector misses or non-radiographs
candidates.statement_a: The audit reads the 71% of known panels without a box as mostly detector misses, because the modality classifier scores 93% on a held-out set.
candidates.quote_a: Only 29% of known panels produced a vertebra box . The modality classifier scores 93% on a held-out set of 2,143 panels, so a large share of the missing 71% is detector miss rather than a panel that is not a radiograph.
candidates.statement_b: The reality check scores nearly half the corpus as not an x-ray at all, and 35% of the level-labelled panels as not spine radiographs.
candidates.quote_b: 8,843 (49%) score as not an x-ray at all. In the released manifest of 17,486 rows, 9,036 sit below the 0.3 floor, 4,218 pass the default inclusion rules, and human_qc_status reads pending on every row. Of the 2,071 decoded panels that carry level labels, 732 (35%) are
candidates.why_it_matters: The two readings point to opposite fixes: detector recall work under the audit, corpus filtering under the reality check; a planner who read only the audit would retrain the detector on a corpus that is half non-radiographs.

candidates.topic: The 2,143-panel held-out set behind the 93% modality score: FluoroCap panels or film-manifest classes
candidates.statement_a: The audit presents the 93% modality score as measured on 2,143 held-out panels and applies it to FluoroCap's missing 71%.
candidates.quote_a: The modality classifier scores 93% on a held-out set of 2,143 panels, so a large share of the missing 71% is detector miss rather than a panel that is not a radiograph.
candidates.statement_b: The reality check says the 2,143 / 800 held-out set is film-manifest classes, not FluoroCap panels, and that modality is unknown for 7,642 of 17,486 manifest rows.
candidates.quote_b: 93.1% modality head / 99.5% view head | | 2,143 / 800 held-out | | film-manifest classes | | not FluoroCap panels; modality is 'unknown' for 7,642 of 17,486 manifest rows
candidates.why_it_matters: The audit's inference about FluoroCap rests on a score measured on a different population; a planner would trust the modality filter on mined figures when it was never tested on them.

candidates.topic: Caption-held-out accuracy of the level model alone, and containment of its level set
candidates.statement_a: The audit (2026-09-14): the level model alone is right 38.3% of the time with the caption held back; containment 56.8% on n = 389.
candidates.quote_a: The level model alone is right 38.3% of the time on panels where the caption was held back. ... 56.8% caption-held-out containment, n = 389
candidates.statement_b: The reality check (2026-09-15): 37.9% on 169 panels; 57.1% containment, Jaccard 0.341, on 380 caption-free panels that are not a random hold-out.
candidates.quote_b: the level model alone is the weakest term in the decoder on real panels (37.9% on 169) ... 57.1% containment, Jaccard 0.341 | | 380 'caption-free' panels | | ... not a random hold-out
candidates.why_it_matters: The sample sizes and values drift between the two pages and the later one says the sample is not a random hold-out, so neither number is a generalisable accuracy; a planner quoting 38.3% or 56.8% from the audit would cite a figure the next day's page withdrew.

candidates.topic: Where every panel comes from: open-licence published figures only, or also surgical video frames
candidates.statement_a: The card asserts every panel is a figure published under an open licence in a peer-reviewed article or on a public repository.
candidates.quote_a: Every panel is a figure already published under an open licence in a peer-reviewed article or on a public repository; no patient record, DICOM header or institutional image was accessed.
candidates.statement_b: The audit of the same day counts 479 surgical video frames in the corpus, mined from surgical video.
candidates.quote_b: The corpus is eleven thousand panel images mined from the literature and from surgical video. ... surgical video frames | | 479
candidates.why_it_matters: A licence tier or a Dataset B release decided from the card's provenance sentence would include video frames the card says do not exist; the card's statement does not describe the corpus the audit counted.

candidates.topic: Provenance of the corpus versus the closed-journal refetch and the Instagram harvest
candidates.statement_a: The card: every panel is an openly licensed published figure, nothing institutional was accessed.
candidates.quote_a: Every panel is a figure already published under an open licence in a peer-reviewed article or on a public repository; no patient record, DICOM header or institutional image was accessed.
candidates.statement_b: The access setup refetches about 600 closed-journal figures through the owner's institutional sign-in and harvests Instagram with a dedicated account against Meta's terms.

verdicts.topic: Figure-mate region agreement with constraint decoding versus the level model alone (same corpus, same date, 2026-09-14)

verdicts.explanation: Both pages are dated 14 Sep. The card's 88% is a string typed into its script, not computed from its data, and it gives no pair count. The card's own data does hold the model-alone figure (468 pairs, 52.1%, recurrent_pred), which matches the audit. Only the decoder figure differs: 88% on the card against 91.5% on 519 pairs in the audit. The card also says the model-alone figure is 'partly induced by the shared caption', but the audit says no caption enters the check. The reality check (15 Sep) repeats 91.5% and 52.1% on 519 and 468 pairs, and labels them model-versus-model agreement.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry 91.5% (519 pairs) for the decoder and 52.1% (468 pairs) for the model alone, as agreement between automatic sources rather than accuracy. Mark the card's 88% as a typed number with no source. Regenerating the card from the decode's consistency file would settle the figure.

verdicts.topic: What the panels without a vertebra box are: detector misses or non-radiographs
verdicts.quote_a: The modality classifier scores 93% on a held-out set of 2,143 panels, so a large share of the missing 71% is detector miss rather than a panel that is not a radiograph.
verdicts.quote_b: The modality classifier scored 18,119 unique panels: 5,665 (31%) more likely a spine radiograph than not, 2,991 (17%) at p ≥ 0.7, 895 (5%) at p ≥ 0.9; 8,843 (49%) score as not an x-ray at all.
verdicts.explanation: The audit (14 Sep) infers that most of the missing panels are detector misses, without scoring them. The reality check (15 Sep) scored 18,119 panels with the classifier (panel_preds.jsonl, read at 07:30): 49% score as not an x-ray, and 35% of the level-labelled decoded panels are not spine radiographs. It also says the 93% was not measured on FluoroCap panels. The corpus grew with the refetch re-split between the two pages, but the later page measured what the earlier one only inferred. Both readings rest on one classifier that was never tested on mined figures.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry the reality check's measured purity, with its file and time, and drop the audit's inference. How much of the no-box set is detector miss stays unmeasured until a human reads a stratified sample of those panels.

verdicts.topic: Provenance of the corpus versus the closed-journal refetch and the Instagram harvest
verdicts.quote_a: Every panel is a figure already published under an open licence in a peer-reviewed article or on a public repository; no patient record, DICOM header or institutional image was accessed.
verdicts.quote_b: The refetch touches only the closed-journal figures that already carry a matched caption (about 600), one request every three seconds per host, capped per day, never full text or PDFs in bulk.
verdicts.explanation: The access setup (14 Sep, afternoon) says closed-journal figures are already in the corpus. It plans to refetch them through the institutional route, and to harvest Instagram under a dedicated account even though Meta's terms forbid automated collection. The overnight report confirms the proxy session served 653 figures and the Instagram route ran. The card's own data also contradicts its blanket open-licence sentence: its routes include reddit (42) and openalex_pdf (41), Dataset A has 246 'unknown' licences, and 166 panels are in tier E. 'Institutional image' in the card means patient images from an institution, not library access, so the conflict is about the open-licence claim and whether the panels can be redistributed.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Withdraw the card's open-licence sentence. Carry the later records: the licence is 'the publishers' (figures)' (registry) and 'figure reuse only, never redistributed' (atlas), and the corpus holds closed-journal copies fetched through the WSU proxy plus Instagram and Reddit images.

verdicts.topic: Rule for sources whose terms forbid automated collection
verdicts.quote_a: Meta's terms prohibit automated collection. Accounts used for it get action-blocked, then disabled. Use a dedicated account, not the one attached to your name or practice.
verdicts.quote_b: never scored; private tracker screening only, never training or a slide; the YouTube copies are unpermitted until a request is answered
verdicts.explanation: The access setup (14 Sep) plans scripted Instagram collection while knowing the terms forbid it. The registry (20 Oct) takes the opposite line. It treats the YouTube copies as unpermitted until the uploader answers, and it records Radiopaedia as 'no scraping' because of its licence terms. The Honest 99 report also left Radiopaedia and Eurorad unscraped because of their AI-training signals. These are two practices for one situation, and the later one is stricter. The registry quotes come from the page source, because the plain-text export cuts off the record array.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry the later rule: no scripted collection where a platform's terms forbid it, and copies already taken are held for private screening only until permission arrives. This matches the project decision that Radiopaedia is never fetched by script. Record a status for the 1,633 Instagram images, which no page gives one.

The atlas (17 Oct) shows the frozen v0.1 A and B exist as internal versions that are 'never redistributed'. So the A/B split survives internally, and the public-release reading is overruled.

verdicts.quote_a: Only 29% of known panels produced a vertebra box .
verdicts.quote_b: The corpus decode (D) behind the recall column: 3,294 panels run, 2,528 with a box, 766 with none, 1,707 with three or more; detection on 17.3% of 19,043 known panels; 12,322 label tokens over 3,027 effective unique panels; decided_by model 1,166, caption 1,100, none 803, VLM 94, OCR 53, mate 43, hardware 34, anchor 1.
verdicts.explanation: Both figures come from the same 14 Sep decode: 3,294 / 11,349 = 29.0% and 3,294 / 19,043 = 17.3%. In each, the numerator is the number of panels run through the decode, not the number with a box (2,528 / 11,349 would be 22.3%). The fall comes from the denominator growing with the refetch re-split before any re-decode, as the reality check says. The detector's coverage did not fall; the corpus outgrew the decode. The audit's wording 'produced a vertebra box' overstates its own number.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry: the 14 Sep decode ran 3,294 panels (29% of the 11,349 on disk then, 17.3% of the 19,043 on 15 Sep), and 2,528 of them had a box. Only a re-decode of the current corpus gives a current coverage figure.

verdicts.topic: VerSeFusion cases with an L6 or T13
verdicts.quote_a: The CT render banks carry roughly a thousand crops each of T10, T11 and T12 and eight hundred of the sacrum; VerSeFusion covers C1 through L6; and 55 VerSeFusion cases carry an L6 or a T13.
verdicts.quote_b: The v2 bank oversamples the 56 VerSeFusion (50 with an L6, 6 with a T13) and 34 CTSpinoPelvic1K cases carrying an L6 or a Castellvi variant: up to twelve poses in two views each, 1,482 frames kept after dropping frames with fewer than two unclipped vertebrae.
verdicts.explanation: The count of 56 with its breakdown supersedes 55, and the reality check supports it: the local VerSeFusion copy holds about 50 L6 scans and 6 T13 files. The Honest 99 report's 85 is the six-lumbar count of raw VerSe20, not of the local VerSeFusion copy; the reality check keeps the two apart. The Honest 99 report also found that the VerSeFusion manifest's T13 flags were wrong, because label 25 means L6 in one scheme and T13 in another.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry 56 local VerSeFusion cases (50 L6, 6 T13) for the v2 bank, and 85 L6 scans in raw VerSe20 as a separate source not yet converted. The distinct-case ceiling for L6 renders is at most 90 (56 + 34).

verdicts.topic: FluoroGen synthetic images: cancelled and unusable, or 12,929 renders kept
verdicts.quote_a: The array was cancelled at 05:50 after 12,896 images, all kept for inspection, none usable for level training.
verdicts.quote_b: synth_rare 12,929 renders over 2,844 cases (T13 86, L6 1,763), 9.0 GB; synth_rare_lowstrength 566; synth_v1 empty
verdicts.explanation: The atlas page source files synth_rare under 'FluoroGen diffusion-styled synthetic frames'. Its note repeats the overnight finding: 'SDXL img2img destroys anatomy at strength 0.45-0.65 and barely changes the DRR at 0.2, and synth_rare is in no bank with no written reason.' synth_rare_lowstrength matches the 300-case low-strength sweep. So the atlas does link the two and agrees the images are unused. Only a gap of 33 images (12,896 against 12,929) is unexplained. The registry, however, gives synth_rare a level truth of 'exact', which the overnight finding contradicts.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry: synth_rare is the output of the cancelled FluoroGen array, kept for inspection and unusable for level training. Correct the registry's 'exact' level truth and write the reason it is in no bank. A file count under [the lab volume's data root]/fluorogen_synthetic would settle 12,896 against 12,929.

verdicts.topic: State of the DRR renderer on 2026-09-15 and 2026-09-16
verdicts.quote_a: Your renderer is already here; check its randomisation list against SyntheX’s before adding anything.
verdicts.quote_b: The scatter term was putting 50–82% of the spine's pixel value into a blurred copy of the bowel beside it, and the photon budget left 0.9 to 12 detected photons at the vertebra — both fluoroscopic settings applied to every render.
verdicts.explanation: Lift (15 Sep) puts the renderer at the DeepDRR physics level, and the reality check of the same day says 'at DeepDRR fidelity already'. A day later the Honest 99 report found scatter and photon-budget defects in every render, and fixed them. So the fidelity claim did not hold for the renders made before the fix. Lift did not recommend skipping renderer work: it recommends auditing the randomisation list and adding off-axis sampling and intensifier distortion. Lift also says its adversarial verification pass never ran.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry the Honest 99 finding: renders made before the fix carry a scatter defect, and fidelity is unmeasured until the matched render-physics comparison reports. Correct Lift's sentence or mark it unverified.

verdicts.topic: Whether the model weights ever left the server
verdicts.quote_a: the model never leaves the server
verdicts.quote_b: | Private forever | Level-identification code, FluoroCap, model weights, spinesurg-ct-nnunet, XRSpinoPelvic1K. Never in a public repository, never on the website. | the website shipped 121 MB of weights until 2026-09-14 |
verdicts.explanation: The map is dated 14 Sep, the day the recipe says the website stopped shipping weights. Its serving lane (weights pulled from a private repository with a read token, 'no model file served' by the website) describes the design from that day on. Read in time the two agree, but the map leaves out that a public copy existed until that day. Neither page says whether the map was made before or after the removal on 14 Sep.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry the serving design together with its history: 121 MB of weights were served publicly until 2026-09-14, and the disclosure audit should treat that copy as exposed.

verdicts.topic: Where the harvest's network traffic runs: WSL or the grid
verdicts.quote_a: the grid's outbound IP is captcha-throttled by PMC; WSL is not
verdicts.quote_b: I will run the closed-journal refetch from the grid login node with a browser-impersonating client before asking you for anything.
verdicts.explanation: The map runs every network route on WSL. The access setup plans the closed-journal refetch from the grid login node, because publishers authenticate the university's address range. The reasons differ (PMC's captcha on the grid against publisher IP authentication), but the chosen hosts conflict. Fetching from the login node also breaks the lab recipe's grid rule 1. The overnight report shows the refetch actually ran from WSL (~/FluoroCap_wsl/refetch_hires.jsonl) through the campus proxy session.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry what ran: network routes on WSL, and closed journals through the WSU proxy session (653 figures). The grid-IP plan was not used. The handoff's rule 10 ('network goes through WSL') is the standing rule.

verdicts.topic: Native resolution of video frames
verdicts.quote_a: Video frames are the only source that is 1080 px native; the current route scrapes search pages and misses most of what the API returns.
verdicts.quote_b: The YouTube route turned 541,621 frame records into 1,462 panels capped at 720p, and Instagram's 1,633 images have no labels at all.
verdicts.explanation: The reality check read the headers of 1,095 video panels with PIL: short side p95 720 px, none at 768 px or above, '720p source'. The 1080 px premise is not what the harvest delivered. The audit mentions a 1080-pixel video refetch covering 141 videos, so some 1080p source may exist, but none shows up in the measured panels.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry the measured 720p cap. Do not use '1080 px native' as a reason to scale video unless a 1080p harvest is measured.

verdicts.topic: Design of the reference standard: two blind readers with adjudication, or one reader
verdicts.quote_a: The protocol specifies two readers blind to each other and to the proposal, adjudication of disagreements by a third, and locking of the dataset, the model and the analysis plan before any performance claim.
verdicts.quote_b: This panel has no caption naming a level. Your read is the only ground truth it will ever have.
verdicts.explanation: The bench stores one read per panel, keyed only by image id, in a shared store (db.doc("reads/"+it.image_id).set(rec)), and loads everyone's reads when it opens. A second reader would therefore see and overwrite the first: the tool can keep neither two blind reads nor a third reader's adjudication. The card's protocol is not what the built tool runs.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Describe the built bench as single-read. Before inter-reader agreement can be reported, reads must be keyed by reader and a separate adjudication pass added.

verdicts.topic: How many panels must be read to turn agreement into accuracy
verdicts.quote_a: Read 400 panels. Nothing else converts an agreement number into an accuracy number.
verdicts.quote_b: The QC's own arithmetic says 545 reads for ±3% around 85%; bounding 99% within ±0.5% takes about 1,500 verified images per stratum you report on (Wilson), and the primary strata are at least four (lumbosacral normal, lumbosacral LSTV, thoracolumbar, hardware).
verdicts.explanation: Both pages agree that 196 reads give ±5% and 545 give ±3%. The audit picked 400 as its action. A day later the reality check sets a two-reader read of the 545-panel set for weeks 1 and 2. Its 1,500 per stratum is a separate target: bounding a 99% claim, which in its design is measured on real Tier 0 frames. The later page raises the FluoroCap read from 400 to 545.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry 545 two-reader, adjudicated FluoroCap reads (±3% around 85%) as the read target, and 1,500 verified vertebrae per primary stratum for any 99% claim. Note that the benches built hold 120 and 179 panels.

verdicts.topic: Sample size of the level verification bench against the stated requirement
verdicts.quote_a: A random sample of decoded panels. 179 panels, 865 vertebrae. This is the measurement, not training data.
verdicts.quote_b: The QC's own arithmetic says 545 reads for ±3% around 85%; bounding 99% within ±0.5% takes about 1,500 verified images per stratum you report on (Wilson), and the primary strata are at least four (lumbosacral normal, lumbosacral LSTV, thoracolumbar, hardware).
verdicts.explanation: The bench claims no precision. 'The measurement' means a random measurement set, as opposed to training data. 179 panels is close to the audit's 196 for ±5%, and the 865 vertebrae are clustered within those panels. The two texts do not conflict; the risk the candidate names lies in how a result might be reported later.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Report the bench's accuracy with a Wilson interval clustered by panel (about ±5%), and state that ±3% needs 545 panels.

verdicts.topic: VinDr-SpineXR's IRB status
verdicts.quote_a: PhysioNet Restricted Health Data License 1.5.0 (named-person DUA); outside WSU determination 2026-269, covered by its supplement HPR 2026-330 (notice 2026-09-29)
verdicts.quote_b: on the grid under a PhysioNet data use agreement that sits outside IRB determination 2026-269 (its own determination pending); dropped from training; only implant boxes used
verdicts.explanation: Both quotes come from the page sources, because the text exports cut off the data. The registry (20 Oct) is the later page but the stale one. Its record cites DATASET_USAGE.md from the 8 Oct handoff, which itself still called the VinDr determination number pending. The atlas (17 Oct) gives the supplement and its notice date, and the repository memory note vindr-is-covered-by-hpr-2026-330 agrees with the atlas.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry the atlas: covered by HPR 2026-330 (notice 2026-09-29). Correct the registry's VinDr record in data/sources.

verdicts.topic: Jecklin 2024 real-image recovery number
verdicts.quote_a: The registered pairs are worth more as labelled fine-tuning data than as anything else: a DRR-only model that collapsed on real frames recovered to F1 0.84 against a 0.86 DRR ceiling with 3,317 registered real crops, and paired pix2pix translation on the same pairs gave the identical 0.84 (Jecklin 2024); where paired and unpaired translation were compared head to head the paired route bought at most one point (86.8% vs 85.8% registration success).
verdicts.quote_b: Outside the project, no paper tests a DRR-trained vertebra-level classifier on real fluoroscopy; the nearest discrete-label precedents lose 26-28 points (Pelphix) and 9 points (SyntheX's lesion task, which is segmentation accuracy, not classification: SyntheX has no classification task), and Jecklin 2024 needed 3,317 pose-paired real frames from 10 cadavers to lift lumbar reconstruction from a surface score of 0.08 back to 0.63-0.73, still below its 0.79 DRR ceiling, with no intermediate sizes tested.
verdicts.explanation: The pages quote two metrics: F1 0.84 against a 0.86 ceiling, and a surface score going from 0.08 to 0.63-0.73 against a 0.79 ceiling. Both may appear in the paper; Lift itself also quotes a surface score ('one case 8% against 76% on its DRR twin'). The texts do not settle whether these measure one quantity. Lift's verification pass never ran, while the reality check's literature claims went through a refutation pass.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Read Jecklin 2024's results table. Until then, prefer the reality check's verified surface-score figures, and name the metric beside each number.

verdicts.topic: Spine-DART 2026 cadaver Dice
verdicts.quote_a: Shape-model fitting from two arbitrary views reaches Dice 0.73 on one cadaver and assumes the level rather than inferring it ( Spine-DART 2026 ).
verdicts.quote_b: Spine-DART's lumbar Mask R-CNN trained on >150,000 DRRs from 377 CTs held Dice 0.82 on 35 real fluoroscopy images of one cadaver against 0.89 on DRRs, a 7-point drop, not the 5 first reported ( pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov );
verdicts.explanation: The pages describe two different results in Spine-DART: a shape-model fit from two views, scored by Dice (0.73), and a 2-D Mask R-CNN segmentation on 35 real frames (0.82 against 0.89 on DRRs). They are not two values for one result. Lift's number did not go through a verification pass.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry both numbers with their tasks named. Check the paper once to confirm that 0.73 belongs to the shape-model fit.

verdicts.topic: Single-crop accuracy on the 8,422 held-out film crops
verdicts.quote_a: 96.7% one vertebra, real films, exact level 8,422 held-out crops · 99.7% within one level
verdicts.quote_b: What your own files prove is much narrower than the morning reports read: one number, 98.7% single-crop on 8,422 held-out cervical and lumbar radiograph crops at 0.17 mm/px with human labels, and nothing else.
verdicts.explanation: Both use the same test set (CSXA 7,440 and NHANES 982 crops) but different models. The ladder's arms ran on 12 and 13 Sep: 96.7% for annotated films at 48 px, 96.9% at 96 px, 97.6% with BUU. The 98.7% (CSXA 99.4%, NHANES 93.6%) belongs to the films-only model deployed on 14 Sep, which the audit (14 Sep) and the reality check (15 Sep) cite. The later pages report a later model.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry 98.7% for the films-only model deployed on 14 Sep and name the model; keep 96.7% as the 13 Sep ladder arm. Whether that model's bank was person-disjoint is the next candidate.

verdicts.topic: Whether the 8,422-crop film validation is person-disjoint
verdicts.quote_a: What your own files prove is much narrower than the morning reports read: one number, 98.7% single-crop on 8,422 held-out cervical and lumbar radiograph crops at 0.17 mm/px with human labels, and nothing else.
verdicts.quote_b: NHANES II entered the banks twice under two names (films\_drr and nhanes\_drr split independently), so 48 of 54 validation persons of the older banks were also in training; found 2026-09-22.
verdicts.explanation: The handoff's list of leaked families is allspine v2, v6 and v7, anchor_drr and vindrps. The films-only model behind 98.7% is not on it, and the reality check pins the nhanes_drr duplication on the all-spine v1 and v2 validation. Neither text says whether the films-only bank carried NHANES under two names.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Look up the films-only model's row in HANDOFF/RESULTS_CATALOG.md and run CHK-2 and CHK-3 on its bank. Until then, cite 98.7% with the note 'person-disjointness not re-verified after the 2026-09-22 leak finding'.

verdicts.topic: YouTube frames harvested
verdicts.quote_a: yt-dlp workers\n197k frames
verdicts.quote_b: outage 07:35–08:05: C: reached 0 bytes free (the WSL virtual disk had grown to 505 GB on 463,977 raw YouTube frames); WSL restarted with a clean journal, 428,606 frames without level evidence deleted (292.6 GB), 32,702 with evidence kept, caches purged; every chain resumed from its ledger; YouTube not restarted
verdicts.explanation: The counts measure different things at different times. Frames on disk were 197k on 14 Sep and 463,977 raw on 15 Sep, cut to 32,702 by deletion. The reality check's 541,621 counts frame records in ledgers, not frames on disk. The atlas tree held 298,075 frames on 17 Oct. The overnight report does explain why the October count is below September's raw count: 428,606 frames were deleted on 15 Sep.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry the atlas's 298,075 frames as current, with the 15 Sep deletion as history and 541,621 as ledger records. Name what each count counts.

verdicts.topic: Castellvi strata in the manifest
verdicts.quote_a: Castellvi strata were requested but never populated: a case-identifier parse in the evaluation failed to join the renders to the manifest, so only normal, L6 and T13 strata exist.
verdicts.quote_b: | 77.8 / 43.4 / 43.7 / 43.1 / 37.1% (normal / Castellvi I-II / III-IV / L6 spines / T13 spines) | | 2,657 renders (ctsp_drr 801, verse_drr 374, physics_rare 1,482) | | CT labels, manifest strata | | no for ctsp_drr and verse_drr; physics_rare renders the same cases |
verdicts.explanation: The reality check reports render accuracies for Castellvi I-II and III-IV strata, and counts 33 Castellvi-graded CTSP1K cases. So the join the audit said had failed was working by 15 Sep (the all-spine v1 transitional test ran at 00:42). The same page says these renders overlap training.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry: Castellvi strata are populated on renders from 15 Sep, with the training-overlap caveat. Real-image Castellvi strata still do not exist.

verdicts.topic: The closed-journal refetch route: grid IP and library access versus the working proxy session
verdicts.quote_a: The library note of 30 June 2026 says DMC residents were dropped from WSU library access.
verdicts.quote_b: The campus proxy session (host-rewrite form) was used on 653 figures and is what made SAGE, Wiley and JNS reachable; 98 figures came from PDFs (Wiley's text-and-data-mining API and open PDFs), identified by content, with the Wiley test case matching the small PMC copy at 0.99 correlation.
verdicts.explanation: The overnight report (15 Sep) answers the access setup's open questions. The owner's credentials authenticated, the proxy session worked, and the refetch did not need the grid-IP route. Wolters Kluwer, Ovid and Thieme still needed a proxy session per host.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry the overnight state: the proxy session works (653 figures), and WK, Ovid and Thieme stay blocked until per-host sessions exist. Treat the access setup's cautions as history.

verdicts.topic: Reader labels: none at the card, still pending on every row a month later
verdicts.quote_a: Status: reader labels pending for every panel.
verdicts.quote_b: Caption-named levels and decoder placements (pseudo); human_qc_status pending on all 21,603 rows.
verdicts.explanation: Both state there are no reader labels: the card on 14 Sep, the atlas on 17 Oct (from the page source). The atlas adds that 'the ~200-panel annotated test set does not exist'. The candidate's '0 verdicts as of 2026-10-22' for the two benches is in neither text, because the bench exports show only the static page and not the stored reads.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry: no FluoroCap panel had a human read as of 17 Oct. Read the benches' stored reads (the artifact database) for the current count before claiming 0 on any later date.

verdicts.topic: The anchor-evidence line of the decoder rests on the anchor_drr bank
verdicts.quote_a: 3,000+ rendered views with every anchor class
verdicts.quote_b: The consequences: allspine v2, v6 and v7, anchor\_drr and vindrps are leaked families, and every number from them is record only, including the 99.02 % shortcut-free film number and the 99 % selective-accuracy claim.
verdicts.explanation: The atlas identifies the anchor detector's bank as anchor_drr, built through slurm/fluorocap_v2.sh and tools/make_anchor_drr.py. Its split puts 301 of 801 CTSP people on both sides, and the handoff (8 Oct) rules anchor_drr a leaked family. The map (14 Sep) presents the route without that caveat, though it makes no accuracy claim of its own.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry the anchor route together with the leak: any anchor-detector score on anchor_drr's validation is record only. Retrain or rescore on a person-disjoint split.

verdicts.topic: Short-side percentile row of the 14 September audit
verdicts.quote_a: The dashed line marks the 320-pixel crop window the level classifier reads; 45.8% of panels fall below 224 pixels and only 7.9% reach 512.
verdicts.explanation: The numbers are identical, and the overnight report names the audit as its source, so this is a sound reuse. The two pages' 'after' rows are a separate candidate.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Keep one copy, attributed to the 14 Sep audit.

verdicts.topic: 2,991 of 18,119 panels pass the modality classifier at p >= 0.7
verdicts.quote_a: The CUT translator finished 30 epochs, but its preview shows what it was trained toward: the panel directories as they are, which include MRI slices, a photographed lightbox and annotated screenshots (the modality classifier calls only 2,991 of 18,119 panels spine radiographs at p ≥ 0.7).
verdicts.quote_b: The modality classifier scored 18,119 unique panels: 5,665 (31%) more likely a spine radiograph than not, 2,991 (17%) at p ≥ 0.7, 895 (5%) at p ≥ 0.9; 8,843 (49%) score as not an x-ray at all.
verdicts.explanation: Both pages carry the same measurement. The reality check names its source (panel_preds.jsonl, read at 07:30), so the missing source line applies only to the overnight report. The classifier was validated on film-manifest classes, so 'classifier-verified' means passed by the classifier, not checked by a human.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Cite 2,991 of 18,119 at p ≥ 0.7 from panel_preds.jsonl, and call these panels classifier-passed rather than verified.

verdicts.topic: The 92.7% v1 render score is a training-set score
verdicts.quote_a: The 92.7% quoted for v1 in the table below was measured on renders whose CT cases were in the training bank and should be read as a training-set score.
verdicts.quote_b: The 92.7% diag is on training cases; L6 100% is 13 training crops; sacrum is 100% on renders and 11.9% caption-free on real panels; the model scores 50-62% on its own cone-beam renders; the films-only model drops to 35.7% on renders, which is the direction of the gap you should expect in reverse.
verdicts.explanation: Both pages carry the same caveat, and they agree. The overnight report's own headline tiles (95.8% at T10, 'L6 13 of 13', 'sacrum 600 of 600') still quote the training-set numbers without it.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Attach the training-set caveat wherever 92.7% or its per-level cells appear, including the overnight report's headline tiles. The render number to carry is 64.2% (v2, held-out renders), which is itself record only under the handoff's leak ruling.

verdicts.topic: 72.8 percent of panels are reproductions with no pixel residual
verdicts.quote_a: Mostly reproductions of published figures (72.8 % of panels have zero pixel residual), so it is a test set at most; dropped from training by directive D1, and the ~200-panel annotated test set does not exist.
verdicts.quote_b: 29,500 figure panels harvested from the literature; 72.8 percent are reproductions with no pixel residual
verdicts.explanation: The figure is duplicated across the two pages; both quotes come from page sources, because the text exports cut off the data. The registry names a record (spine-program 01_carm_level_detection/DATA.md; data_platform DATA_MANIFEST.md defect 35) and the atlas says 'found in repository'. Neither states the method, the residual threshold or the run.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Name the script, threshold and output file behind 72.8% (it should be in DATA_MANIFEST.md defect 35) before the book cites it.

verdicts.topic: Literature results on synthetic-to-real transfer (DeepDRR 78.2 to 24.7 mm, SyntheX 5.95 vs 6.46 mm)
verdicts.quote_a: (1) Physics in the renderer: naive DRRs to DeepDRR took landmark error on real cadaver films from 78.2 to 24.7 mm ( Unberath 2019 ); strong domain randomisation on 10,000 DRRs from 20 CTs beat training on the 366 real frames (5.95 vs 6.46 mm) and CycleGAN or ADDA added nothing on top (SyntheX).
verdicts.quote_b: Physics matters more than volume at the start: the same landmark network went from 78.2 mm to 24.7 mm mean error on 78 real cadaver X-rays when naive DRRs were replaced by DeepDRRs, most of the gain arriving before scatter was added ("Enabling machine learning in X-ray-based procedures via realistic simulation of image formation", pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov ).
verdicts.explanation: The 78.2 to 24.7 mm result matches on both pages. The SyntheX 5.95 against 6.46 mm also appears on both, but the reality check's verified text corrects Lift's reading of it. It says the scaled set is reported as both 10,000 and 18,000 images, and that 'scale rather than the strong-randomisation list is what carried the win'. So the shared block agrees on the numbers but not on what SyntheX shows.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry the reality check's verified wording for SyntheX: scale, 10,000 or 18,000 images, and a scaling curve that is not monotone. Correct Lift's unverified attribution of the win to strong randomisation.

verdicts.topic: The manifest regenerates byte-identical from the same inputs
verdicts.quote_a: Search protocol, query strings in eleven languages, routes and thresholds are written down; the manifest is regenerated by one command from the fetched material and is byte-identical for identical inputs.
verdicts.quote_b: the manifest regenerates byte-identical from the same inputs
verdicts.explanation: Both pages assert the property. Neither names the command or a run that tested it. The card names only tools/fluorocap_report_stats.py, which writes the card, and records one manifest hash (980e007b...) for its own 10,281-row manifest. The 17,486-row and 21,603-row manifests that followed are different manifests.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Record the regeneration command and one run that reproduced a frozen manifest's SHA-256 (for example the v0.1 lock) before the book states the property.

verdicts.topic: The grid's outbound IP is captcha-throttled by PMC and publishers authenticate by IP
verdicts.quote_a: the grid's outbound IP is captcha-throttled by PMC; WSL is not
verdicts.quote_b: The grid is inside the university's address space ([the university's network range]) and publishers authenticate by IP.
verdicts.explanation: Neither page cites a recorded test. The access setup says its one probe that day was 'inconclusive only because Wolters Kluwer refuses plain clients outright'. The overnight report shows the refetch went through the proxy session instead.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Record a probe (PMC from the grid against WSL, and one publisher from the grid IP) before the book states either claim. Otherwise state only the route that ran: WSL plus the WSU proxy.

verdicts.topic: The printed label beside the vertebra is the strongest anchor
verdicts.quote_a: authors print 'L4' beside the vertebra; the strongest anchor there is, and a pointer to vertebrae the detector missed
verdicts.quote_b: The caption's "L4" was, in most figures, assigned by the author counting on a limited field.
verdicts.explanation: The map's claim has no source. The reality check's sentence is about the caption's level, not a printed label, but both are levels the author assigned by counting. The reality check also calls printed level labels (3.6% of 2,815 scanned panels) a leak a network will learn. The audit's script data gives printed-level OCR 53.8% caption-held-out containment on n = 13, below figure mates, captions, the VLM and hardware. That is the only measurement, and as far as it goes it contradicts 'strongest'.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Drop 'strongest anchor' unless a read measures how accurate printed labels are. Cite the audit's 53.8% (n = 13) as the only measurement, and call it agreement, not accuracy.

verdicts.topic: A whole-run-correct panel should be the common case on the level verification bench
verdicts.quote_a: Use a to mark every box on a panel right when the whole run is correct, which should be the common case and makes this fast.
verdicts.quote_b: the level model alone is the weakest term in the decoder on real panels (37.9% on 169)
verdicts.explanation: Nothing measured supports the bench's expectation. The reality check's figures do not prove the opposite either: they come from a selected caption-free subset and measure containment or a single decider, not whether a whole run is correct on a random sample. Still, the expectation has no basis, and the one-key shortcut invites readers to accept the model's names.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Remove 'which should be the common case' from the bench instructions, or replace it with the measured rate once the bench has reads.

canonical_check.why: The reality check (2026-09-15) re-measures every quantity the audit (2026-09-14) reports, on the refetched corpus of 19,581 images instead of 11,349, and says measurements outrank the morning report; its box rate (17.3% vs 29%), caption-held-out numbers (37.9%/57.1% vs 38.3%/56.8%), modality reading (49% not an x-ray vs detector miss) and Castellvi strata replace the audit's. The audit keeps content the reality check does not repeat (per-level recall, hardware constraints, renderer fixes, the 400-panel read plan), so it is superseded for its numbers, not deleted as a source.

The reality check explicitly supersedes the overnight report's counts (19,048 images, 1,489 refetched, 927 video panels) and says measurements outrank the morning report, so the overnight report is canonical only for what the reality check does not cover; but its 08:30 update postdates the reality check's 06:55 to 07:15 snapshot on the v2 model (registered 08:13, 64.2% on 800 renders) and on the CUT v2 job ids, so on those two items the overnight report is the later record. A superseded relation from overnight-report to reality-check, with the v2 items excepted, fits the records better than two canonical pages.

The card is a frozen 2026-09-14 09:43 view (10,281 rows, dataset 0.2) whose counts, figure-mate number (88%) and provenance sentence are contradicted the same day by the audit and superseded by the reality check (17,486 rows) and the atlas (21,603 rows, 29,500 panels); its licence tiers and release framing conflict with the later private-forever rule. It stays canonical for the licence tiers, inclusion and exclusion rules and the reader protocol, not for counts or release intent.

No later page redraws the pipeline, so the map remains the one description of the routes; its counts (197k frames, manifest v0.3) and its network and serving invariants are dated or contradicted (the access setup's grid plan, the lab recipe's 121 MB of shipped weights, the handoff's anchor_drr leak), so a reader takes its structure and not its numbers.

clusters.unsourced_summary: The dataset card and the pipeline map both assert that the manifest regenerates byte-identical from the same inputs and that an unbroken SHA-256 chain runs from original figure to weights, naming no command, run or checksum file. The map asserts that the grid's outbound IP is captcha-throttled by PMC while WSL is not, and the access setup asserts that publishers authenticate by IP from the university's address space; neither cites a probe, and the overnight report shows the refetch ran through the proxy session instead. The access setup asserts that video frames are the only 1080 px native source and that Instagram serves posts at 1080 px wide, with no measurement; the reality check says the YouTube panels came capped at 720p. The map's anchor panel asserts that an author's printed label is the strongest anchor there is, with no accuracy measured for printed labels, while the reality check says the caption's label was mostly assigned by counting on a limited field. The atlas and the registry both state that 72.8 percent of the 29,500 panels are reproductions with no pixel residual, naming no duplicate-detection run or threshold. The card's 88% figure-mate number carries no pair count. Lift Before Label asserts the renderer is already at the DeepDRR/SyntheX level with no test, and its own adversarial pass never ran. The adjudication bench asserts that the reader's single read is the only ground truth the panel will ever have, and the level verification bench assumes a whole-run-correct panel is the common case; neither assumption is measured, and the card's protocol promises two blind readers with a third adjudicating. The reality check's claims that 'Castellvi I is two thirds of transitional anatomy' and that registration-derived labels are biased are stated without a source in the records.
clusters.stale_summary: All six primary pages are snapshots of 14 to 15 September 2026 with running work inside them: the card says dataset version 0.2 with 0.3 in progress and reader labels pending for every panel; the pipeline map draws manifest v0.3 and 197k YouTube frames; the access setup says the PMC refetch is running now and worries about a library note of 30 June 2026; the overnight report says round two of the refetch is still running, the FluoroGen array was cancelled at 05:50, the CUT v2 is queued as jobs 40285316/7 and the v2 retrain registered at 08:13; the reality check, read between 06:55 and 07:15, says the v2 weights were destroyed and retrain 40285209 is pending, lists CUT jobs 40285274 and 40285275 as queued, and lays out a 90-day and 12-month plan from 15 September. The Honest 99 report of 16 September says training on the enlarged corpus, the backbone comparison and the render-physics test were still running. Later pages date them: the atlas of 2026-10-17 shows human_qc_status pending on all 21,603 rows and the two benches show 0 of 0 verified as of 2026-10-22, so the card's 'reader labels: none yet' still holds five weeks on; the handoff of 2026-10-08 says 14 cine sources, SX-Stitch and Balgrist requests are drafted and none sent, 0 verified real-frame transitional persons against 35 needed, and the registry of 2026-10-20 still calls VinDr's determination pending although the atlas three days earlier says HPR 2026-330 covers it (notice 2026-09-29) and the YouTube copies unpermitted until a request is answered. The lab recipe of 2026-09-27 says the website shipped weights until 2026-09-14. The CNS talk window (31 October to 4 November 2026) and the Radiopaedia USD 250 fee in the records are unconfirmed as of the records' dates.
clusters.notes: Quotes for the primary pages, the Honest 99 report, the handoff, the lab recipe, Lift Before Label, the level context ladder, the OR ledger and the three benches were checked against the plain texts; the extracted texts of fluoroscopy-data-atlas and schwingnet-data-registry truncate their embedded JSON and returned no hits for their key numbers, so those two artifacts are quoted from their inventory records only. Two of the readers' quotes named the university's network range, for which an editor's words now stand; no e-mail address, phone number or home address appears, and people are named by role (the owner, the reader). The FluoroGen 12,896 versus synth_rare 12,929 pair may be two different objects; it is listed because no page says so. The overnight report's 08:30 update postdating the reality check's snapshot is why the clustering's two canonical pages disagree on the v2 model state. Several secondary artifacts (Honest 99, handoff, registry, atlas) carry the later word on the corpus and the directive, so a reader of the canonical set alone would miss the private-forever rule, the leaked-family ruling and the October counts.

verdicts.quote_b: On held-out radiographs the detector finds 99.2% of vertebrae. Three misses in 243
verdicts.explanation: Both pages are dated 2026-09-18 and describe the same held-out real-film test with the same sentence: three misses in 243, two of them the sacrum. Naming Vertebrae Without CT says the detector finds 97.6%, while Vertebral Levels Without CT says 99.2%. Three of 243 is 98.8%, which matches neither.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry 'three misses in 243 (two the sacrum)' and no percentage until the detector's evaluation file is read.

verdicts.topic: Detector miss rate on held-out film: 2.42% or 2.2%
verdicts.quote_a: the miss rate is 2.42% at confidence 0.25, 0.10 and 0.05 alike
verdicts.quote_b: it misses only 2.2% of vertebrae — but 17.9% come out duplicated
verdicts.explanation: Naming's 2.42% agrees with Vertebral Levels' own threshold table (2.4% at each threshold). Vertebral Levels' 2.2% with 17.9% duplication sits in a paragraph about the detector on 25 held-out radiographs used for sweep chains, and the page does not say it is the same set. Naming reports duplication differently, as 3.03% within frames and 21.8% across frames.
verdicts.resolution_hint: The detector evaluation record for each set (the 243-vertebra test and the 25-film sweep set) would settle which miss rate goes with which; carry 2.4% for the threshold test meanwhile.

verdicts.topic: Number of lumbar real films in the per-region table (24 or 25)
verdicts.quote_a: Lumbar real films, n=24 78.7% alone 93.6% swept
verdicts.quote_b: 78.7% without the sweep · n=25 films
verdicts.explanation: Naming Vertebrae Without CT's chart and Vertebral Levels Without CT's own chart both give the lumbar real-film row as n=24 at 78.7% alone and 93.6% swept. Vertebral Levels' headline tile gives the same 78.7% at n=25 films. One page holds two n's for one row.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry n=24 (both charts) provisionally; the evaluation record behind the row would settle it.

verdicts.topic: How many images carry a sacrum box (4,526 or 5,110)
verdicts.quote_a: Trained on the 4,526 images that carry a sacrum box, single class, split by patient: precision 98.2%, recall 96.9%
verdicts.quote_b: 5,110 images carry a sacrum box and zero carry an S1 box
verdicts.explanation: Naming Vertebrae Without CT (2026-09-18) says the sacrum detector was trained on 4,526 images that carry a sacrum box, and its limits section says 5,110 images carry a sacrum box. The page does not reconcile the two: 4,526 may be the training side of a patient split of 5,110, or a different snapshot.
verdicts.resolution_hint: The sacrum bank's manifest (total and per-split image counts) would settle it.

verdicts.topic: How many VerSe or VerSeFusion scans have an L6
verdicts.quote_a: 56 VerSeFusion (50 with an L6, 6 with a T13)
verdicts.quote_b: VerSe scans with L6: 85 scans (Liebl 2021) against 47 cases (Sekuboyina 2021) and 87 read series. No file has counted from the masks.

The State of the Literature (2026-10-08) lists VerSe L6 as 85, 47 or 87 and unresolved, and Research Directions lists the count as '85, 47, 50 or 87', with three files disagreeing. The Reality Check explains 50 as the local VerSeFusion copy against VerSe20's 85, but no file counts from the masks.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry 85 (Liebl 2021, published) and 50 (the local VerSeFusion copy) separately; the raw-mask count planned as CT-3 would settle it.

verdicts.topic: How many CTSpinoPelvic1K cases have an L6
verdicts.quote_a: CTSpinoPelvic1K L6: 18 by release label, 16 by the readers' own count, 29 persons in the registry.
verdicts.quote_b: 802 crops from at most 90 distinct cases (56 VerSe + 34 CTSP)

The State of the Literature's own disagreement (18, 16 or 29) is real but internal to it.

verdicts.topic: CTSpinoPelvic1K record count: 802 or 801 persons
verdicts.quote_a: 802 records, one per patient; 422 supine, 377 prone
verdicts.quote_b: 301 of 801 persons on both sides
verdicts.explanation: Research Directions (2026-10-08) says CTSpinoPelvic1K v11 has 802 records, one per patient, split 422 supine and 377 prone; those parts sum to 799. The same-day handoff counts 801 persons, Counting From The Sacrum gives 801 distinct subjects, and Research Directions itself also writes '801 of 802'. The records disagree on whether there are 802 or 801 persons.

verdicts.topic: Level-model accuracy on L6 crops of six-lumbar spines
verdicts.quote_a: called L5 in 41 of 68
verdicts.quote_b: was 0% yesterday; called L5 in 366 of 913
verdicts.explanation: The audit (2026-09-14) scores the deployed films-only model at 0.0% on 68 L6 render crops, 41 of them called L5. The overnight report (2026-09-15) scores a new all-spine v1 model, trained overnight on films plus every CT render source, at 46.4% on 913 crops, and notes that it 'was 0% yesterday'. The model changed, contrary to the candidate's reading. The same report adds v2 held out at 63.0% single-crop (68 of 108), with the decoder calling 39.8% L6.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry the overnight report's held-out v2 figures (63.0% single-crop on 108, 39.8% by the decoder) with their model named, noting that v1's 46.4% was not held out and that all of these predate the leak audit.

verdicts.topic: L6 accuracy after real six-lumbar images entered training
verdicts.quote_a: 83 real clinical images of six-lumbar spines entered training and accuracy at that vertebra went from 67.4% to 73.5% on held-out patients
verdicts.quote_b: The best rendered L6 recall is 56.1 to 72.4 % on ten held-out persons.
verdicts.explanation: Naming Vertebrae Without CT (2026-09-18) reports L6 accuracy rising from 67.4% to 73.5% on held-out patients; Vertebral Levels gives 67% to 73% on 105 held-out patients. Research Directions (2026-10-08) gives the best rendered L6 recall as 56.1 to 72.4% on ten held-out persons, with zero verified real-frame transitional test persons. The sets, metrics and banks differ, and the October page neither mentions the September figure nor says whether its patients were held out under the later person split.
verdicts.resolution_hint: The results-catalog row for the 73.5% (its bank, split and whether its 105 patients are held out under G3) would settle it; meanwhile carry 56.1 to 72.4% on ten held-out persons from Research Directions.

verdicts.topic: Whether any real L6 image existed in training in mid-September
verdicts.quote_a: 0 panels labelled; 0 real-film crops
verdicts.quote_b: L6 has 213 and T13 has 73, and until this week almost every one of those was simulated from a CT rather than photographed
verdicts.explanation: The Reality Check (2026-09-15) finds no real image labelled L6 and no real-film L6 crop. Naming Vertebrae Without CT (2026-09-18) lists 213 L6 training patients, 83 of them real radiographs, and says that until this week almost all were simulated, so it records a change made after the Reality Check. Neither page says where the 83 came from or whether a human verified them.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry Naming's 83 real L6 training images as added between 15 and 18 September with unstated provenance and verification, beside the October records' zero verified real-frame transitional test persons.

The two records disagree on whether FluoroCap is in training.

verdicts.topic: FluoroCap as a source of verified transitional panels

The audit's 2 of 2,815 (2026-09-14) counts caption text mentioning transitional terms, and the overnight report says the decoders could insert L6 or T13 only from 2026-09-15. These are different measures, and neither claims a human read.

verdicts.topic: FluoroCap panel count: 20,700 decoded (16 Sep) vs 29,484/29,500 (22 Sep, 8 Oct)

verdicts.topic: Figures replaced by publisher originals in the refetch

verdicts.topic: Level model alone on caption-held-out real panels
verdicts.quote_a: The level model alone is right 38.3% of the time on panels where the caption was held back.

verdicts.topic: allspine v2 own-validation accuracy (78.8 vs 78.5) and cone-beam/rare splits
verdicts.quote_a: Own validation 78.8% exact, 95.9% within one, 97.2% region

verdicts.topic: The honest v1 render number: 92.7% (training) vs 64.2% held-out vs 35.7%
verdicts.quote_a: over 800 held-out renders it scores 64.2% , with 4,505 training renders skipped. That is the honest render number.

In the overnight report (2026-09-15), 92.7% is all-spine v1 on renders of training cases, and 64.2% over 800 held-out renders is the retrained v2, not v1 as the candidate says. They differ by model, not only by which renders were skipped.

verdicts.topic: Castellvi type I as about two thirds (68%) of all LSTV
verdicts.quote_a: It is about two thirds of all transitional anatomy
verdicts.quote_b: Castellvi type I is a coronal transverse-process height of 19 mm or more, 68 % of all LSTV

Research Directions does give one: its CT-3 gate expects type I near 68% of calls and names Hanhivaara 2020 prevalence as the outside check. The Reality Check traces 68% to 3,855 abdominal CTs, of which 68% of LSTV were type I. So the figure is sourced, though for one cohort rather than all LSTV.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry '68% of LSTV were Castellvi type I in 3,855 abdominal CTs (Hanhivaara 2020)' from the Reality Check, scoped to that cohort.

verdicts.topic: Prevalence of a sixth lumbar vertebra (roughly 2% vs 3.2% prior vs 2.0% measured)
verdicts.quote_a: A sixth lumbar vertebra occurs in roughly 2% of people
verdicts.quote_b: L6 3.2 % and four lumbar 1.6 % (Sun 2025)
verdicts.explanation: Counting Against Two Anchors (undated) gives roughly 2% with no source. The State of the Literature (2026-10-08) is sourced: it gives the 3.2% prior from Sun 2025 and a measured CTSpinoPelvic1K rate of 2.0% (Wilson 1.3 to 3.3%). The anchors page's 2% agrees with the measured rate, so the claim is neither shared-unsourced nor in real disagreement.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry the 3.2% prior (Sun 2025) and the 2.0% measured on CTSpinoPelvic1K (Wilson 1.3 to 3.3%) from the State of the Literature.

verdicts.topic: LevelCheck's accuracy as a comparator (100%, 99.998% registration, or voted down)
verdicts.quote_a: | 99.998% — LevelCheck | | registration converged: the fraction of trials whose mean projection distance was under 5 mm. It moves with computing budget — 100% at 200 restarts, 99.3% at 50 — which is the signature of a convergence rate | | no |
verdicts.quote_b: the 'registration-based tools report near-perfect accuracy' summary (Otake 99.99%, Lo 100%/99.3%, Vaishnav 100%) were both voted down, so the registration-based ceiling and the registration-free floor are both unquantified here
verdicts.explanation: The feasibility study voted down the reading of these figures as near-perfect identification accuracy, and so left the registration-based ceiling unquantified. Vertebral Levels Without CT, three days later and from a verified search, says the same figures are registration convergence, not naming ('Is it naming? no'). Both pages give the clinical 100% as labels inside the correct level on 398 radiographs, conditional on correct CT labels and after exclusions. Both give the 42.2% utility as a three-surgeon mean with range 31.7 to 53.3%, and the feasibility study explains the 157 versus 168 sum by that averaging. Neither page uses these figures as naming accuracy, so there is no disagreement; the skeptic took the vote against the accuracy reading as a vote against the numbers. One correction to the re-checker's hint: the feasibility study says Huang 2022's 88.3% did not survive verification, so that figure is not settled.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry the table from Vertebral Levels Without CT: 99.998%, 100% and 99.3% are registration convergence; the clinical 100% is conditional label placement on 398 radiographs after 21 exclusions; 42.2% is a three-surgeon mean (range 31.7 to 53.3%); none is naming accuracy. The one naming figure with a human is 97.6% on 62 hard films. Carry the registration-free 88.3% only with the feasibility study's note that it did not survive that study's verification.

first.quote_a: It moves with computing budget — 100% at 200 restarts, 99.3% at 50 — which is the signature of a convergence rate
first.quote_b: the 'registration-based tools report near-perfect accuracy' summary (Otake 99.99%, Lo 100%/99.3%, Vaishnav 100%) were both voted down
first.explanation: Vertebral Levels Without CT (2026-09-18) presents LevelCheck's 99.998% and its 100% / 99.3% as registration convergence rates checked against their sources. The feasibility study (2026-09-15; its caveats are rendered one character per line) says that same near-perfect summary was voted down. It keeps only labels within the correct level on all 398 radiographs after 21 exclusions, and a 42.2% helpfulness whose region parts sum to 157, not 168. The pages agree that none of these is naming accuracy but disagree on whether the registration figures survived verification.
first.resolution_hint: Carry the feasibility study's verified LevelCheck facts (labels in the correct level on 398 radiographs after 21 exclusions; helpful in 42.2% as a three-surgeon mean), and keep 99.998%, 100% and 99.3% out unless re-verified.

verdicts.topic: The 97.6% comparator cannot be exceeded at any reachable n
verdicts.quote_a: the comparator 97.6 % cannot be exceeded at any reachable n
verdicts.quote_b: LevelCheck H2, superiority over 97.6 % | as H1 | 0 below 152 persons at any accuracy | 708 at a true 99 %; never at 98 %
verdicts.explanation: Both pages are dated 2026-10-08 and both make the claim, but the State of the Literature gives its basis in the power table: zero power below 152 persons, 708 needed at a true 99%, never reached at 98%. Research Directions repeats 152 and 708. The calculation is on the page, and both name the same paper-2 comparator against registration-assisted surgeons.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry the claim with the State of the Literature's H2 power row as its basis, and the comparator as Manbachi 2018's 97.6% assisted reading of 62 hard films (Research Directions).

verdicts.topic: Kwak 2025 LSTV classifier: 76.4% on 313 held-out films or on 3,116
verdicts.quote_a: accuracy 76.4%, sensitivity 85.1%, specificity 61.9%, AUC 0.84 on 313 held-out films (166/195 LSTV, 73/118 normal)

verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry 76.4% and AUC 0.84 on 313 held-out films (3,116 in the dataset) from the feasibility study.

verdicts.topic: Leakage between fine-tune banks and the fixed test on 2026-09-22

The handoff's 48 of 54 is the NHANES II double entry in the older level-encoder banks (allspine v2, v6, v7). These are different banks, so both can hold on the same day.

verdicts.topic: Near-duplicate and person leakage: zero pairs vs 92 of 97 transitional persons in training
verdicts.quote_a: 0 pairs ≥ 0.97 against 37,165 film images, 29,484 FluoroCap panels, 1,445 yolo_v6f

Research Directions' 92 of 97 is a person-level count of transitional validation and test persons inside the v8 and v9 encoder training lineage. They answer different questions and do not conflict.

verdicts.topic: Owner's rule of no synthetic data generation versus render-based training
verdicts.quote_a: No synthetic data generation. Your instruction, and the learning curve agrees: flat past forty positives.
verdicts.quote_b: renders raise film naming 6 to 22 points at 5 to 25 persons
verdicts.explanation: The Honest 99% page (2026-09-16) lists 'No synthetic data generation' among what it did not do, yet its own headline is measured on held-out renders, and the same list keeps 'No full re-render' separate. So the rule as recorded there does not exclude CT renders. Later records keep renders in training as the only labelled L6 and T13. The page does not define the rule's scope further.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry the owner's rule as recorded on the Honest 99% page, noting that renders were in use the same night; the directive's own record would define its scope.

verdicts.topic: How many human reads the verification needs
verdicts.quote_a: 196 adjudicated panels for ±5%, 545 for ±3%
verdicts.quote_b: A 99 % selective-accuracy claim | 2,956 answered held-out renders | not a power calculation | about 298 answered cases; 2,673 for class-conditional 99 % at 27 classes
verdicts.explanation: The audit's 196 and 545 are reads to estimate true panel accuracy to within ±5% or ±3%. The State of the Literature's 298 and 2,673 are for a 99% selective-accuracy claim. The Reality Check's 1,500 per stratum bounds 99% within ±0.5%, and the Honest 99% page's 99 per class is for class-conditional guarantees. Each page states its own target, so they do not disagree.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry each requirement with its stated target and do not compare them as one number.

verdicts.topic: Stratum size needed vs the adjudication bench's 120 panels over 31 strata
verdicts.quote_a: bounding 99% within ±0.5% takes about 1,500 verified images per stratum you report on (Wilson)
verdicts.quote_b: 120 panels drawn stratified across deciding evidence and spinal region.
verdicts.explanation: The Reality Check's 1,500 is for bounding a 99% claim within ±0.5% in each reported primary stratum, and the same page lists the 120-panel reading set b1 as built and unread. The bench page does not claim per-stratum accuracies, and its manifest spreads 120 panels over 31 strata. The pages do not disagree.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry the bench as a 120-panel stratified sample (about four per stratum) that can give neither per-stratum nor 99% bounds.

verdicts.topic: Reader protocol: two blind readers with a third adjudicator, or a single reader as the only ground truth
verdicts.quote_a: The protocol specifies two readers blind to each other and to the proposal, adjudication of disagreements by a third
verdicts.quote_b: This panel has no caption naming a level. Your read is the only ground truth it will ever have.
verdicts.explanation: The dataset card (2026-09-14) specifies two blind readers and a third adjudicator. verdicts.topic: Best published whole-spine identification accuracy

verdicts.topic: What COBRA2026 is: 867 patients from six centres and two vendors, or 145 patients from four centres on Elekta

The 145 is the cases in the bank, not the dataset.

These are bank and subset counts that agree with a; the person count, 3,600 or 1,200 patients, is a's own open disagreement, which b does not address.

verdicts.topic: COBRA2026 sacrum detection by the fixed detector: 80% held-out near-AP or 3.4% of frames

The detectors, frames and measures all differ.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry both, each labelled: 80.0% exact among 240 scored at 41.9% coverage (ledger), and 3.4% sacrum found by paper 2's frozen detector (State of the Literature).

clusters.unsourced_summary: The cluster asserts a number of things with no source in any record. The clinical-need lines in Naming Vertebrae Without CT and Vertebral Levels Without CT (half of surveyed neurosurgeons report a wrong-level operation; 15 of 100 consecutive discectomies; 179 fiducial placements over 38 months at 52 minutes and 183 mGy) carry no citation in either page. Counting from the Sacrum states that published class-agnostic C-arm detection reaches 0.96 to 0.98 and that the best published registration-free naming is 73.3% importing identity from a preoperative radiograph, with no paper named, and declares the naming problem solved to a standard nobody has published; Ninety-three Pixels says no per-vertebra recall on real fluoroscopy is published and that the 71.67% has no peer, and that LevelCheck's 100% imports identity from the patient's own CT; Research Directions says no lumbosacral 3-D classifier exists at all. The Castellvi type I share (about two thirds in the Honest 99% page, 68% in Research Directions) and the sixth-lumbar prevalence of roughly 2% with a 97%-correct four-lumbar prior (Counting Against Two Anchors) are stated without sources, and the handoff itself says every planning value assumed 95 to 99% that no measurement supports. The handoff and the state-of-the-literature record both say the 97.6% comparator cannot be exceeded at any reachable n, without the calculation, and one calls it a LevelCheck figure and the other a reader figure. The OR-readiness ledger asserts that surgeons centre the field the same way every time and that FluoroCap's article list has no DeepFluoro, C-ArmLSpine, COBRA or Geneva paper, neither shown. The Honest 99% page says every number comes from a named file on the grid but names none, and the overnight report says three independent checks were run without naming them; the lab recipe tallies that 0 of 79 manifest keys begin with a job id. The level bench calls model-decided panels the common case with no count behind it. The REFORMS checklist states the grid's bash 4.2 and Python 3.6 and that a DOI cannot be withdrawn, both unsupported. The LSTV bench's modality and family guesses are machine guesses whose method is not stated.
clusters.stale_summary: As of 2026-10-22 the three benches (SchwingNet/level-verification-bench-mkjxsy, undated; SchwingNet/lstv-verification-bench-6m2qhr, 15 September 2026, pass one; SchwingNet/fluorocap-adjudication-bench-rnsyir, batch b1 from decode_v2_v2.jsonl) all show zero verdicts, and the October 8 records (Research Directions, the state of the literature, the handoff) say the verified real-frame transitional test count is zero. The FluoroCap chain is a sequence of same-week snapshots: the corpus audit (2026-09-14, 11,349 images, no human read), the dataset card (generated 2026-09-14 09:43, v0.1 frozen, v0.3 in progress, reader labels pending for every panel), the overnight report (2026-09-15, updated 08:30, MORNING_REPORT.md to be written, CUT v2 jobs queued), the reality check (2026-09-15 06:55 to 07:35, v2 retrain 40285209 pending, translator jobs queued, reading_set_b1 and reading_v2 built unread, 4,218 empty reader rows, a 90-day and 12-month plan) and the Honest 99% page (2026-09-16, counts against yesterday morning, ordinal-loss arm running, benches awaiting the owner), whose headline the October handoff marks record only. The narrative pages of 2026-09-18 (Naming, Vertebral Levels) have a 376-case CV running, a sacrum detector being built, a tolerant rule in testing and are themselves a post-leak rewrite that the later 92-of-97 audit overtakes. Ninety-three Pixels (2026-09-21) has eight GPU jobs running and a re-render decision left to the owner; the OR-readiness ledger (2026-09-22, re-scored 06:50) has ws_mixed 40411495 running, device fits in progress, the clean DeepFluoro retrain 40411934, a crop re-score pending and the styled corpus queued; Counting from the Sacrum (2026-09-22) has row (d) rendering, an A/B pending on a sampler implemented but not adopted, the fleet detector training on 18,906 frames and the CTSP1K id-is-person audit running, and the handoff says nothing after 2026-09-27 changed the banks. The feasibility study's deep-learning comparator is from October 2025. The lab recipe (2026-09-27) records the public mirror still at v10 and a pelvis DECISION.json never produced; the REFORMS checklist (2026-10-03) says none of its 32 gates exists. The October 8 records leave the dataset-request letters drafted and none sent, CHK-6 and CHK-7 never run, the leak check failing on a stale Geneva fixture, the provisional not recorded as filed against the 30 October deadline, and CNS on 31 October to 4 November 2026. Counting Against Two Anchors is an undated spec whose five arms are not run.
clusters.notes: The clustering gave no superseded or duplicate relations, so canonical_check is empty; the records themselves imply several the clustering omitted: the reality check (2026-09-15) explicitly supersedes the overnight report's image count (19,581 over 19,048); the OR-readiness ledger's 06:50 re-score supersedes its own 06:10 recall figure; Naming Vertebrae Without CT and Vertebral Levels Without CT are two tellings of one 2026-09-18 experiment with shared tables and the same confidentiality line, and the second says an earlier version was superseded after the leak audit; the handoff and Research Directions (2026-10-08) retire the Honest 99% page's headline as record only; Research Directions, the state of the literature and the handoff are one account's one-day audit repeated three times. All quotes are drawn from the inventory records; the plain-text files were not needed. Two number collisions are worth a warning rather than a candidate: 35.7% is both the v1 level model's accuracy on CT renders (audit, reality check) and the coverage at which the Honest 99% page reaches 99%, and 67.4% is both the majority-vote baseline that the sweep lifts to 91.8% and the L6 baseline that 83 real images lift to 73.5%. Several contradictions may be different scoring sets rather than errors (DeepFluoro seed spread, C2 on real, the 8,422-vertebra level-as-class row, count-alone 97.0 vs 99.96), and the why_it_matters says so where the quote does not fix the set. People are named by role (the owner, first and second account); literature authors are cited as the records cite them.
