verdicts.topic: VinDr-SpineXR access route (credentialed vs restricted)
verdicts.quote_a: VinDr-SpineXR requires a personal PhysioNet credentialed account — CITI training plus supervisor attestation, typically weeks.
verdicts.quote_b: One correction to the earlier report. VinDr-SpineXR was described as needing PhysioNet credentialing (CITI training, supervisor sign-off, weeks). It does not. It is a restricted -access dataset: register on PhysioNet, sign the Data Use Agreement, download. Same day.
verdicts.explanation: The field report (undated) says VinDr-SpineXR needs a credentialed PhysioNet account, which takes weeks. The X-ray data handoff, checked on 3 September 2026, names that report as earlier and corrects it: the dataset is restricted access, under the PhysioNet Restricted Health Data DUA 1.5.0, and can be had the same day. The board of 2026-09-11 also lists VinDr as PhysioNet Restricted 1.5.0.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry the handoff's statement: VinDr-SpineXR is restricted access, needing a registered user and a signed DUA (PhysioNet Restricted Health Data DUA 1.5.0), obtainable the same day.

verdicts.topic: How many CSXA API endpoints were tried
verdicts.quote_a: the 4,963 images sit behind a SciDB browser session; four candidate API endpoints all returned errors.
verdicts.quote_b: Eight guessed API endpoints were tried ( sdb-file/file/list , sdb-core/dataSetFile/list , sdb-open/dataset/… and others); all returned errors.
verdicts.explanation: Both pages describe the same failed attempt to download CSXA from Science Data Bank. The field report counts four endpoints. The handoff of 2026-09-03 follows that report: it quotes the report's own line, says its failure text comes from the run's log, and counts eight. It does not say outright that the four was wrong.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry eight guessed endpoints from the X-ray data handoff (2026-09-03), which was checked against the grid and the run log. Note that the field report said four.

verdicts.topic: Network architecture: one network with four heads vs separate models
verdicts.quote_a: One network, four heads — not separate models, not one flat class list
verdicts.quote_b: single-vertebra ResNets on 96 px targets with a marker channel; BiGRU run labeller per model and rung; flip TTA; entropy for the queue
verdicts.explanation: The decisions page marks a shared backbone as locked, with detection plus keypoints, level, lesion and Cobb heads. The board of 2026-09-11 says the same. The FluoroCap map of 2026-09-14 builds separate models: a YOLO11 pose corner detector, a 4-model level ensemble of single-vertebra ResNets with a BiGRU, and a separate orientation net. The handoff of 2026-10-08 likewise lists five separately trained pieces. No page says the locked decision was revised.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry the built system as the handoff (2026-10-08) describes it: separate detectors, an encoder and a recurrent head. Record one network with four heads as the earlier locked design, which was not implemented.

verdicts.topic: Sacrum model: own model vs shared head
verdicts.quote_a: Give the sacrum its own model. It is not a four-cornered body and should not be asked of a model trained on four-cornered bodies.
verdicts.quote_b: One network, four heads — not separate models, not one flat class list
verdicts.explanation: The naming note of 18 September 2026 decides on a separate single-class sacrum detector, trained on 4,526 images. The decisions page, contemporary with the board of 2026-09-11, locks one network with heads and 'not separate models'. Neither page refers to the other's choice.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry the separate sacrum detector of the naming note (2026-09-18) as the later design, and record the one-network decision as superseded in practice. The handoff's 2026-10-08 list of pieces supports separate detectors.

verdicts.topic: Level identity: morphology vs counting vs coupling
verdicts.quote_a: Name from morphology, never from a count.
verdicts.quote_b: The proposal is to count, not to name. ... nothing learned decides the level.
verdicts.explanation: The naming note (2026-09-18) names each vertebra from its appearance and says nothing is counted. The counting-levels proposal (September 2026, citing runs of 21 September) states the opposite principle: count from an anchor, with no name formed. The handoff (2026-10-08) and the research directions combine the two: 'the count alone names 97.0 %' and coupling adds 1.2 points.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry the latest account, from the handoff and research directions of 2026-10-08: per-vertebra naming plus a count from the detected sacrum, with disagreement as the stop signal. State that the earlier pages took opposite single principles.

verdicts.topic: Held-out-device per-vertebra detection recall on C-ArmLSpine
verdicts.quote_a: Under the matched convention the C-ArmLSpine-held-out vertebra recall is 90.6%.
verdicts.quote_b: held-out-device detection recall 80.5 %; same-device plateau about 84 %
verdicts.explanation: The OR ledger (2026-09-22) re-scored 56 whole C-ArmLSpine frames (287 vertebrae) at outline IoU 0.5 and conf 0.25 and got 90.6%. The handoff (2026-10-08) catalogs held-out-device recall at 80.5% and says its results catalog wins wherever another file differs. The any-view plan (2026-10-21) repeats 80.5%, and 84.0% with 24 device frames added. Neither later page states the truth convention.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry 80.5% held-out-device recall, and about 84% with device frames, from the handoff's results catalog. Keep 90.6% only as the ledger's earlier matched-convention rescore, and read the catalog row for its convention.

verdicts.topic: Render-only detection on C-ArmLSpine whole frames
verdicts.quote_a: | Detection from renders alone | | 0.3% |
verdicts.quote_b: The render-only detector reads 31.7% outline / 54.7% centre.
verdicts.explanation: The OR ledger (2026-09-22) gives the render-only detector on 56 C-ArmLSpine whole frames several values: 17.1% vertebra recall in its device table, 2.4% by body IoU in the rescore, 31.7% by outline and 54.7% by the centre rule. The ledger disagrees with itself on the body-box value. The any-view plan (2026-10-21) gives 0.3%, with no convention, threshold or render generation.
verdicts.resolution_hint: The results catalog row for render-only detection on C-ArmLSpine, giving its truth convention, threshold and render generation, would decide which value to carry.

verdicts.topic: Population-matched sacrum recall on DeepFluoro real frames
verdicts.quote_a: A detector trained on renders of DeepFluoro's own CTs finds the sacrum on 90–97% of the real frames, six specimens held out in turn.
verdicts.quote_b: A detector trained only on calibrated renders of DeepFluoro's own CTs finds the sacrum on about 96–98% of real frames (leave-one-specimen-out).
verdicts.explanation: Both pages describe the same population-matched experiment. The counting-levels proposal (September 2026; leave-one-specimen-out runs of 21 September) reports 90–97% in its table of 6 specimens with 3 seeds each. The AIDaS proposal (October 2026) copies much of that text but gives about 96–98% and names no run. The OR ledger separately gives 88.5–91.3% for one specimen's clean render-only number.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry 90–97% from counting-levels, which is tied to the 21 September runs and the report tool, unless the leave-one-specimen-out report shows the 96–98% that AIDaS gives.

verdicts.topic: Share of a real frame's variance explained by physics alone
verdicts.quote_a: our renderer explains 80.9% of a real frame's variance; nine calibrated device terms add 4.3 points, held out by specimen
verdicts.quote_b: The stored DeepFluoro frames also turned out to be log-compressed display images; read correctly, physics alone explains 86% of a real frame rather than 80%, and the calibrated renderer about 90% of a held-out one.
verdicts.explanation: The ninety-three-pixels board (2026-09-21) gives 80.9% and +4.3. The counting-levels proposal (September 2026) corrects the physics-only share to 86% and the calibrated renderer to about 90%, after finding that the stored frames were log-compressed. The AIDaS proposal is later (October 2026, due 16 October) yet still carries the uncorrected 80.9% and +4.3. So the later page is the stale one.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry 86% from physics alone and about 90% from the calibrated renderer, per the counting-levels correction. Mark 80.9% and +4.3 as figures from before the frames were read correctly.

verdicts.topic: Whether the residual after physics has local structure
verdicts.quote_a: what is left is a smooth per-frame field with nothing local in it — 0.4% of variance at ≤2 px
verdicts.quote_b: "Nothing local" was too strong ... After the field, the 2–16 px bands sit at 0.1–0.8% of the frame's variance each — two to seven times the noise floor, not at it.
verdicts.explanation: The what-is-left page (dated only 2026) quotes the ninety-three-pixels claim (2026-09-21) and takes it apart on four real frames. It refers to that board's 76.9%, so it plainly follows it, and it marks the 'nothing local' part as too strong.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry the what-is-left reading: after the smooth field, the 2–16 px bands hold 0.1–0.8% of variance each, two to seven times the noise floor.

verdicts.topic: Gain from calibrated device terms on the Cios Fusion
verdicts.quote_a: Scatter width boxed to 6–16 px: +4.3 , 15.8 px with spread 0.4, every term stable — the calibration now applied.
verdicts.quote_b: | Siemens Cios Fusion (DeepFluoro) | | 366 | | 0.899 → 0.905 (+1.3) |
verdicts.explanation: Ninety-three-pixels (2026-09-21) gives 80.9% attenuation variance explained (NCC 0.899), and a held-out gain from the nine device terms of +4.1 median, +4.3 with scatter boxed. The OR ledger (2026-09-22) device card labels 0.899 → 0.905 (+1.3) as 'held-out R² physics → fitted', from a new fit that it says reproduces the shipped calibration. The two pages seem to use different metrics, and the +1.3 does not equal 0.905 minus 0.899.
verdicts.resolution_hint: The Cios Fusion device card and the fit's definition of its gain metric (R², NCC or variance explained, in points) would show whether +1.3 and +4.3 measure the same thing.

verdicts.topic: Which devices have fitted cards
verdicts.quote_a: | Varian Halcyon | | 10 | | 1.7% | | 98.3% |
verdicts.quote_b: The per-device parametric styling claim: no device has been fitted beyond the Cios Fusion, and no styled corpus exists.
verdicts.explanation: Both pages are dated 2026-09-22. The ledger, at 06:10 EDT, lists device fits still running, a Varian OBI queued for COBRA, and the BV Pulsera already marked fitted. The counting-from-the-sacrum page reports that day's audit of cards for six devices, a Varian Halcyon among them. The two may reflect different hours of one day.
verdicts.resolution_hint: The timestamps of the device card files, and the time the counting-from-the-sacrum page was written, would settle which devices had fitted cards on 2026-09-22.

verdicts.quote_a: Zero-shot , lateral no C-ArmLSpine data in training at all | | 96.27%
verdicts.quote_b: | Naming, lateral, encoder that saw the device only through renders | | 96.4% (595/617) |

verdicts.quote_b: | Naming, AP, zero-shot | | 43.7% | | A one-level cranial shift: a counting error, not an appearance error.

verdicts.topic: Fine-tuned whole-frame lateral naming on C-ArmLSpine
verdicts.quote_a: 98.2% exact level on whole C-ArmLSpine lateral frames, five-fold CV over 148 cases [95.7–100]; 92.9% with three vertebrae in the field, 72.8% with one
verdicts.quote_b: 97.4 % of bodies named on a whole lateral frame and 74.8 % with one body in view
verdicts.explanation: The OR ledger and counting-from-the-sacrum (2026-09-22) give 98.2% (98.22%), and 72.8% with one vertebra. The handoff (2026-10-08) catalogs 97.4% and 74.8% and says its catalog wins where any file differs. Research directions and the any-view plan repeat 97.4%. Neither later page says why the value moved; the person-disjoint split of 2026-09-23 falls between the dates.

verdicts.topic: The Ljubljana set(s)
verdicts.quote_a: | Ljubljana 2D/3D gold standard | | held | | 18 frames, 1 cadaver | | L1–L5 |
verdicts.quote_b: it added the Ljubljana angiographic set (10 patients, 3-D DSA + posed frames)
verdicts.explanation: The OR ledger lists two different Ljubljana sets: an angiographic set of 10 patients, and an 18-pair 'Trixell PIXIUM 4600 (Ljubljana turntable, not a C-arm)'. The any-view plan's 18 frames from 1 cadaver matches the turntable set. Research directions also describes one cadaveric L1 to L5 with gold pose.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry them as two sets: the 18-frame, one-cadaver 2D/3D gold standard (any-view, ledger) and the 10-patient angiographic set (ledger).

verdicts.topic: Published per-vertebra detection on real C-arm frames
verdicts.quote_a: published class-agnostic C-arm detection reaches 0.96–0.98
verdicts.quote_b: No per-vertebra recall on real fluoroscopy is published at all.
verdicts.explanation: Counting-from-the-sacrum (2026-09-22) cites a published C-arm detection range with no paper and no metric. Ninety-three-pixels (2026-09-21) says no per-vertebra recall on real fluoroscopy is published, and calls its own 76.9% the first. If the 0.96–0.98 is an AP or mAP figure, or comes from frames that are not real fluoroscopy, the two do not conflict.
verdicts.resolution_hint: The citation and the metric behind 'published class-agnostic C-arm detection reaches 0.96–0.98' would settle whether a published per-vertebra recall exists.

verdicts.topic: Best published registration-free naming accuracy
verdicts.quote_a: The best published registration-free naming is 73.3%, and it imports identity from a preoperative radiograph.
verdicts.quote_b: | Published registration-free network, cadaveric long films | | no | | correct level named | | 88.3% |
verdicts.explanation: The naming note (2026-09-18) gives a published registration-free network on cadaveric long films at 88.3%. Counting-from-the-sacrum (2026-09-22) calls 73.3% the best published registration-free naming, in a passage about real intraoperative C-arm frames. Neither names the paper, so it is unclear whether the two figures cover different tasks.
verdicts.resolution_hint: The two papers' citations and test settings (intraoperative frames or cadaveric long films) would show whether 73.3% is the best on intraoperative frames and 88.3% a different task.

verdicts.topic: LevelCheck / registration comparator accuracy
verdicts.quote_a: LevelCheck (Lo et al., Spine 2015, 20 thoracolumbar surgery patients, 10,000 perturbed views) labelled 100% of views correctly at about 26 s, and 99.3% at 7 s.
verdicts.quote_b: | CT-to-fluoroscopy registration (LevelCheck line) | | yes | | registration converged — not naming | | 99.998% |
verdicts.explanation: The pages report different measures. The naming note says its 99.998% is registration convergence, 'not naming'. The any-view plan reports the share of perturbed views labelled correctly, at two run times. The 97.6% is the surgeon-with-CT-overlay figure, a third measure.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry each figure with its measure: 99.998% convergence (naming note), 100% at 26 s and 99.3% at 7 s view labelling (any-view, citing Lo 2015), and 97.6% assisted surgeons.

verdicts.topic: T13 example count in training
verdicts.quote_a: T13 73 65 of them are real radiographs; the rest are simulated from CT
verdicts.quote_b: | T13 | 22 carriers, about 55 people in total | 7 persons in all sources, 0 real | 0 |
verdicts.explanation: The naming note (2026-09-18) counts 73 distinct T13 training patients, 65 of them real radiographs. Research directions (2026-10-08) gives 7 T13 persons in all sources and 0 real. In its table, 22 carriers is the pre-stated n a gate needs, not a count, so the candidate's reading of 22 is wrong. The handoff's registry gives T13 14.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry research directions' 7 T13 persons in all sources, 0 verified real (2026-10-08). Do not carry 22 as a count, and treat the naming note's 65 real as unverified training labels.

verdicts.topic: L6 example count
verdicts.quote_a: L4 has 11,062; L6 has 213 and T13 has 73
verdicts.quote_b: L6 18 by label and 16 by the readers; four-lumbar 9
verdicts.explanation: The figures have different scopes. The naming note counts distinct training patients per level across every source, CT-simulated ones included (83 real for L6). Research directions' 18 and 16 are CTSpinoPelvic1K v11 alone, and the handoff's 146 is the anomaly registry. Within that one cohort, the decisions page's 'about 22 of 802' differs from v11's 18 by label.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry each number with its scope. For CTSpinoPelvic1K, carry v11's 18 by label and 16 by the readers from research directions.

verdicts.topic: Lumbar rib count in CTSpinoPelvic1K
verdicts.quote_a: The model never memorises sixteen lumbar-rib examples in order to recognise one.
verdicts.quote_b: that marked L1 rib‑bearing in 61 cases where the strict incidence QC found only 14 lumbar ribs in the entire cohort.
verdicts.explanation: The two-anchors page (undated) gives sixteen lumbar-rib examples, 'measured on the released labels'. The rib audit finds 14 lumbar ribs by strict incidence QC, while its table counts 21 (v4) and 25 (v5) ribs kept on a lumbar vertebra. The pages mix ribs and cases, and label versions, without saying which.
verdicts.resolution_hint: A count by case, on a named label version (v5), of cases with a rib on a lumbar vertebra would settle it.

verdicts.topic: C3 coverage across sources
verdicts.quote_a: C3 appears only in CSXA, T7 only in AASCE.
verdicts.quote_b: Cervical is now covered by CSXA and NHANES independently
verdicts.explanation: The decisions page says both, and the board of 2026-09-11 does too. The X-ray data handoff lists NHANES annotation as per-level masks for C2–C7 and T1, so C3 is not only in CSXA.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Drop 'C3 appears only in CSXA'. Carry that named cervical levels come from both CSXA (C3–C7) and NHANES (C2–C7), per the X-ray handoff.

verdicts.topic: T12 vs L1 classifier (AUC 0.990): single-vertebra shape or patient-normalised features
verdicts.quote_a: T12 separates from L1 at AUC 0.990 and 97.3% accuracy over 1485 vertebrae, using shape alone with each patient's own size divided out.
verdicts.quote_b: The published 0.990 for T12 against L1 divides five of its eleven features by the patient's median over three or more levels, so it is not a single-vertebra classifier
verdicts.explanation: The two-anchors sentence itself goes on to say the features have the patient's own size divided out. That is research directions' point, so on what the 0.990 is, the pages agree. The two remaining differences are 1485 against 1,486 vertebrae (from 798 cases), and that two-anchors uses the figure to argue a per-vertebra head is learnable, which research directions rejects.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry research directions' description (2026-10-08): AUC 0.990 on 1,486 vertebrae from 798 cases, normalised within the patient, and not a single-vertebra classifier.

verdicts.topic: CT patch size for the segmentation network
verdicts.quote_a: A tall narrow patch, 112 × 112 × 320 at 1 mm, spans the column in 4.01 Mvox — cheaper than nnU-Net's default 192³ at 7.08.
verdicts.quote_b: a plan built for 100 GB of VRAM — patch 384×256×256, batch 2 — died in the first forward pass.
verdicts.explanation: The board's patch belongs to the nnU-Net plan of the CT folds that were running on 2026-09-11. The two-anchors patch is proposed for a different design, the ordinal-head arms. They are different networks, not one setting reported two ways.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry both, each with its network: 384×256×256 for the running nnU-Net folds (board), and 112×112×320 proposed for the anchor-ordinal arms (two-anchors).

verdicts.topic: AASCE film count
verdicts.quote_a: | AASCE / SpineWeb | | 579 |
verdicts.quote_b: AASCE (481, AP scoliosis) and Mendeley (591): AP or no levels; not used.

verdicts.quote_a: | Mendeley | | 716 |
verdicts.quote_b: Mendeley (591)

verdicts.topic: VinDr-SpineXR lesion classes
verdicts.quote_a: Annotation Lesion boxes, 13 types — no vertebra labels
verdicts.quote_b: 19,551 lesion boxes across 7 detectable classes
verdicts.explanation: The X-ray handoff (2026-09-03) says 13 lesion types, and the decisions page says 7 detectable classes. The word 'detectable' may mark a subset of the 13, but neither page says so.
verdicts.resolution_hint: VinDr-SpineXR's own class list, and how its 13 annotated types map to the 7 detection classes, would settle it.

verdicts.topic: BUU-LSPINE film count
verdicts.quote_a: BUU — 77 of ~7,200 files. Google Drive caps folder downloads; the rest needs per-file IDs or rclone.
verdicts.quote_b: | BUU-LSPINE | | 7,204 |
verdicts.explanation: The field report's 77 files were a partial download, and the X-ray handoff of 2026-09-03 marks it superseded. The board (2026-09-11) shows full BUU being normalised, and the decisions page lists 7,204 on the grid. The ladder and the any-view census give 7,203 films from 3,600 people.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry the full release now held: about 7,200 films from 3,600 people (7,203 per the ladder and the any-view census, 7,204 per decisions). The one-film difference is unresolved.

verdicts.topic: Detector training-set size
verdicts.quote_a: 958 images · 6073 instances · 727 patients · ... YOLO11m-pose, one class, four keypoints, 1024 px, AdamW, 111 epochs on one H200. ... python -m src.run_eval --weights runs/pose/runs/detect_v1/weights/best.pt
verdicts.quote_b: | Body detector (YOLO11m-pose) | zoomed film windows from CSXA, BUU AP and lateral, and the 543 annotated NHANES films: 12,709 films, with no written reason for the other 26,996 held films | the naming boxes |
verdicts.explanation: The field report (undated) is a run report for the stage-1 one-class detector detect_v1. That run trained 111 epochs on 958 images from NHANES II, Mendeley and a partial BUU download, at a time when CSXA was still out of reach. The handoff (2026-10-08) gives the training set of a different, later model, detector_v5z_final: 12,709 films including CSXA. It never mentions detect_v1 or the 958 images. The handoff does not revise the field report's figure, which is still true for detect_v1. The two pages describe two model versions, so the candidate's supersession does not hold. The skeptic's own explanation calls them different generations, which is a version difference, not a revision.
verdicts.resolution_hint: From the handoff, carry 12,709 films as the training set of the current body detector, detector_v5z_final. From the field report, carry 958 images, 6,073 instances and 727 patients as detect_v1's, the first one-class stage-1 run, so its metrics are never read as the current detector's.

first.quote_b: 12,709 films, with no written reason for the other 26,996 held films
first.explanation: These are different detector generations. The field report's stage-1 detector trained on 958 images. Decisions gives 4,327 images for the 0.991 model, and ninety-three-pixels cuts its arms from 11,007 labelled films. The handoff (2026-10-08) gives the current body detector as trained on 12,709 films.
first.resolution_hint: Carry 12,709 films for the current body detector, from the handoff, and name the earlier generations with their sizes.

verdicts.topic: Film detector mAP / recall
verdicts.quote_a: 0.957 AP@50 · held-out test
verdicts.quote_b: The model that scores mAP50 0.991 today was trained on 4,327 images
verdicts.explanation: The field report's 0.957 belongs to the 958-image stage-1 model. The decisions page, which postdates the board of 2026-09-11 because it records the IRB purge done, gives mAP50 0.991 and PCK@0.1 0.812 for a model trained on 4,327 images. Ninety-three-pixels' 0.991 is a recall, a different metric.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry mAP50 0.991 and PCK@0.1 0.812 for the 4,327-image model, from decisions, naming the model, and keep 0.957 as the earlier stage-1 result.

verdicts.topic: Render-trained detector recall on real DeepFluoro frames
verdicts.quote_a: finds the sacrum on 76.9% of 365 real frames pooled over all six specimens (by specimen 47.8–96.2%)
verdicts.quote_b: The manuscript's 76.9% belongs to the anchor_none_r2 generation; the v2 generation every real fine-tune started from pools to 64.0%.
verdicts.explanation: The OR ledger (2026-09-22) does not withdraw 76.9%. It ties 76.9% to the anchor_none_r2 generation and gives 64.0% for another, v2. Counting-levels' '64% / 77%' for two renderings is consistent with this. The 0.740 is the cranial C2 detector's recall, and 71.67% is render-only recall on real radiographs; both are different quantities.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry 76.9% labelled as the anchor_none_r2 generation and 64.0% as the v2 generation, per the OR ledger.

verdicts.topic: Whether oblique views are measured
verdicts.quote_a: Obliques are unmeasured.
verdicts.explanation: The naming note (2026-09-18) measured oblique renders on 89 spines, where naming falls to about 58%. Research directions (2026-10-08) cites per-angle naming of 82.1% at trained angles and 52.8% elsewhere. The any-view plan (2026-10-21) says obliques are unmeasured and does not limit that to real frames.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry that oblique renders have been measured (naming note; research directions' 82.1% and 52.8%) and that real oblique frames have not. Qualify the any-view line accordingly.

verdicts.topic: Orientation handling
verdicts.quote_a: Inversion and a 180° flip break every detector at once (orientation is assumed, not inferred).
verdicts.quote_b: sideways frames rotated; an upside-down call makes the decoder try both orders
verdicts.explanation: The ledger's statement is about the OR detectors under corruption tests on C-ArmLSpine frames. The 4-way orientation net is a preprocessing step in the FluoroCap pipeline for published-figure panels. Different pipelines, both statements true.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry both with their scope: the OR path assumes orientation (ledger, 2026-09-22), and the FluoroCap panel pipeline infers it (map, 2026-09-14).

verdicts.topic: Effect of resolution and collimation on detection
verdicts.quote_a: Flat. 836 px to 139 px costs 0.00 points of per-vertebra recall.
verdicts.quote_b: fine-tuned on zoomed windows because collimated frames broke the film-trained scale
verdicts.explanation: Ninety-three-pixels downsamples whole films, changing the pixel count but not the anatomy's scale in the frame. The FluoroCap map, and the OR ledger's crops at 36% and 19%, concern magnification. The ledger says 'Scale is a device-transfer lever of its own'.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry both: resolution costs nothing on films (ninety-three-pixels), while magnified, collimated fields cost recall (FluoroCap map, OR ledger).

verdicts.topic: Leakage between training banks and test sets
verdicts.quote_a: 0 pairs ≥ 0.97 against 37,165 film images, 29,484 FluoroCap panels, 1,445 yolo_v6f
verdicts.quote_b: NHANES II entered the banks twice under two names (films\_drr and nhanes\_drr split independently), so 48 of 54 validation persons of the older banks were also in training; found 2026-09-22.
verdicts.explanation: The ledger checks the real OR test frames (C-ArmLSpine, DeepFluoro, COBRA) against the external corpora by image similarity. The handoff's two leaks are person-level, inside the film and CT render banks' own splits. These are different checks on different sets, so they do not conflict.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry both with scope: no near-duplicates of OR test frames (ledger), and two person-level bank leaks fixed by the G3 split of 2026-09-23 (handoff).

verdicts.topic: CTSpinoPelvic1K: one id per person?
verdicts.quote_a: If two ids are one human being then the corpus is mis-split, and that would be larger than either data leak already found and fixed. An audit is running; it is not assumed to be fine.
verdicts.quote_b: 802 records, one per patient; 422 supine, 377 prone
verdicts.explanation: Counting-from-the-sacrum (2026-09-22) leaves open whether a record is a person. Research directions (2026-10-08) states one record per patient, and lists 351 prone and supine pairs as second acquisitions in a separate project. Its 422 supine plus 377 prone makes 799, leaving three records unaccounted for.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry one record per patient from research directions (2026-10-08). The posture split is incomplete (799 of 802).

verdicts.topic: Target size of the retraining set
verdicts.quote_a: from 4,327 training images toward ~13,500
verdicts.quote_b: trained on 4,327 → retraining on ~34,000
verdicts.explanation: The board (2026-09-11) aims at about 13,500 images, while about 22,000 radiographs were being normalised. The decisions page plainly follows the board: it records as done the IRB purge the board was waiting on, totals 50,887 annotated images, and gives about 34,000 as the retraining target.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry about 34,000 from decisions as the later target. The current detector's actual set is 12,709 films (handoff, 2026-10-08).

verdicts.topic: Sacral slope in the v11 spinopelvic table
verdicts.quote_b: the v11 sacral slope 36.6 against Veilleux 36.5
verdicts.explanation: The board (2026-09-11) gives table II with n 563 and SS 33.2. The handoff (2026-10-08) gives the v11 release value of 36.6. Research directions says the SS 33.1 estimator note predates the plate fix of 2026-09-11, and that its 3.4-degree gap to Veilleux is 0.1 on v11.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry v11 sacral slope 36.6 from the handoff and research directions, with the version named.

verdicts.topic: How many lumbar films with level labels are in training
verdicts.quote_a: about 380 lumbar films with annotated levels exist in training, against ~5,000 cervical
verdicts.quote_b: L4 has 11,062; L6 has 213 and T13 has 73, and until this week almost every one of those was simulated from a CT rather than photographed.
verdicts.explanation: The ladder (2026-09-13) counts real lumbar films with annotated levels. The naming note (2026-09-18) counts distinct training patients per level, CT-simulated and counting-inferred sources included, and calls them 'populations rather than crops'. Different units and scopes.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry each with its scope: about 380 annotated real lumbar films (ladder), and 11,062 L4 training patients from all sources, simulated included (naming note).

verdicts.topic: Status of DRR-supplied level identity / render-to-fluoro translation
verdicts.quote_a: No published work uses DRRs to supply level identity to a 2D model
verdicts.quote_b: | Render-to-fluoro translation (SDXL, CUT, CycleGAN, ADDA) | no gain in any arm | refuted |
verdicts.explanation: The board makes a literature-novelty claim about using DRRs for level supervision. Research directions refutes image-translation restyling arms. These are different claims, and neither contradicts the other.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry them separately. The novelty claim stays unsourced (see candidate 61), and the translation arms are refuted (research directions).

verdicts.topic: LSTV / transitional prevalence figures
verdicts.quote_a: 3,461 normal / 15 lumbarization / 130 sacralization — 4.0% prevalence
verdicts.quote_b: The 93.3 / 3.3 / 3.3 distribution above should not be quoted as a phenotype prevalence.
verdicts.explanation: The figures come from different cohorts and quantities. The board's are BUU radiograph labels. The rib audit counts non-rib-bearing vertebrae in CTSpinoPelvic1K, says that count mostly reflects the label convention, and says it is not a prevalence. Research directions' 9 to 11% is Castellvi II to IV on CT, a third definition.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry each with its cohort and definition, and quote no prevalence from the rib audit's distribution.

verdicts.topic: C2 as a counting anchor
verdicts.quote_a: counting from C2 on whole‑spine imaging is the only definitive method
verdicts.quote_b: C2 detected 0–8% on real films (25 truths)
verdicts.explanation: The rib audit's statement is about the clinical reference standard for vertebral identity on lumbosacral CT. The OR ledger's figure is a detector's C2 recall on real films. The two do not conflict.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry both separately, each as a statement of its own kind.

verdicts.topic: Counting-grade claim
verdicts.quote_a: Twelve arms of 16 to 801 spines each lie between 99.17 and 100%.
verdicts.quote_b: Counting-grade (≥97%) detection on a device held out entirely: best clean numbers are 84% sacrum / 91% vertebrae (C-ArmLSpine)
verdicts.explanation: Counting-levels scores how exact the count is 'with the annotation's vertebra boxes', and itself calls deployment a detection question. The OR ledger's 'not supported' is about detection on a device held out entirely. Different stages of the pipeline.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry both: the count is exact at 99.17–100% given correct boxes, and held-out-device detection is not yet counting grade.

verdicts.topic: FluoroCap in training sets
verdicts.quote_a: FluoroCap is out of training; the IRB umbrella covers only public de-identified data downloadable without an agreement.
verdicts.quote_b: The C-ArmLSpine fold models behind the fine-tuned naming numbers still train on 2,632 VinDr crops and 2,100 FluoroCap crops per fold bank, plus both NHANES copies
verdicts.explanation: The handoff (2026-10-08) states the directive, says its fold banks break it, and adds 'That contradicts the directive'. Research directions says FluoroCap is dropped by directive and in no training list, which is the plan, not the state of the fold banks.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry the open defect: the fine-tuned numbers rest on fold banks that hold FluoroCap and VinDr crops. The handoff notes that fold models without them already exist (the name_fill cells).

verdicts.topic: Real-film held-out naming (8,422 crops)
verdicts.quote_a: 96.7% one vertebra, real films, exact level 8,422 held-out crops · 99.7% within one level
verdicts.quote_b: | This work, one frame, no sweep | | nothing | | 97.0% | | 0% |
verdicts.explanation: The ladder's 96.7% is its 48 px arm. Its 96 px arm reads 96.9% overall, with regions 97.6/95.5/85.4/93.5. The naming note's 97.0% on 1,653 films and 8,422 vertebrae carries exactly that regional row, so the remaining gap is 96.9% against 97.0% on the same crops, perhaps rounding.
verdicts.resolution_hint: The ladder's per-crop result file for the 96 px one-vertebra arm would give the exact fraction to carry (96.9% or 97.0%).

verdicts.topic: Spinal-AI2024 decision
verdicts.quote_a: All rights reserved by default, and GAN-derived from an upstream corpus whose terms it inherits. Do not download.
verdicts.quote_b: Spinal-AI2024 pulled despite having no licence file
verdicts.explanation: The board (2026-09-11) advises against downloading Spinal-AI2024. The decisions page follows the board: it records the board's pending IRB purge as done, and says the owner made the call to pull the set, tagged research-track, with the status 'revisit'.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry the later state from decisions: Spinal-AI2024 is held, research-track only, with its licence to be revisited.

verdicts.topic: Number of decisions in the decisions artifact
verdicts.quote_a: Twelve decisions across the paper, the network architecture, the data and the governance
verdicts.quote_b: IRB correspondence purged from public history
verdicts.explanation: The page's decision headings run from 'One network, four heads' to 'IRB correspondence purged from public history': nine decisions. They are followed by one open question (L6 Dice 0.00). The page's own count of twelve does not match.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry nine decisions and one open question, as the page itemises them.

verdicts.topic: Field report reproduce command vs trained epochs
verdicts.quote_a: python -m src.train --epochs 120 # fliplr=0.0, mosaic=0.0
verdicts.quote_b: YOLO11m-pose, one class, four keypoints, 1024 px, AdamW, 111 epochs on one H200.
verdicts.explanation: The field report's reproduce command asks for 120 epochs, and its trained model and curve stop at 111. The page does not say whether training stopped early or was cut.
verdicts.resolution_hint: The run's results.csv, which the page says it was generated from, would show whether 111 was an early stop within a 120-epoch run.

verdicts.topic: Sacrum box count vs evaluated images
verdicts.quote_a: So the sacrum gets its own detector. Trained on the 4,526 images that carry a sacrum box, single class, split by patient: precision 98.2%, recall 96.9% .
verdicts.quote_b: 5,110 images carry a sacrum box and zero carry an S1 box
verdicts.explanation: The naming note (2026-09-18) gives two counts of images carrying a sacrum box, 4,526 and 5,110. It does not explain the difference, for example a later count or a different subset.
verdicts.resolution_hint: The crop-bank manifest of the sacrum detector would give the number of images that carry a sacrum box, and say which set the 98.2% and 96.9% were measured on.

verdicts.topic: Within-three-levels accuracy in the ladder
verdicts.quote_a: 7,900 crops, CSXA + NHANES · 99.5% at three
verdicts.quote_b: Cervical: one vertebra 97.7%, three 99.3%, five 99.5%.
verdicts.explanation: The ladder's headline chip says 99.5% with three vertebrae visible. Its body text and full table give cervical 99.3% at three and 99.5% at five.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry cervical 99.3% at three vertebrae and 99.5% at five, from the ladder's table.

verdicts.topic: DeepFluoro frame and specimen counts
verdicts.quote_a: finds the sacrum on 76.9% of 365 real frames pooled over all six specimens
verdicts.quote_b: 3,094 real frames: COBRA Elekta train and validation (118 cases) and DeepFluoro (5 specimens), initialised from a TotalSegmentator-render detector
verdicts.explanation: The handoff's 5 specimens are what the vertebra and sacrum detector trained on. The dataset is 6 specimens and 366 frames; ninety-three-pixels itself says 366 frames over 6 specimens, and the ledger splits them 4/1/1. The 365 is the pooled count scored in ninety-three-pixels' per-specimen table, which is one frame short and unexplained.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry DeepFluoro as 6 specimens and 366 frames, 5 specimens in the detector's training (handoff), and 365 frames scored for the 76.9%.

verdicts.topic: CTSpinoPelvic1K record count
verdicts.quote_a: The CT axis named 802 abdominopelvic records ... CTSpinoPelvic1K 801
verdicts.quote_b: About 22 of 802 cases carry an L6 at all, roughly 2.7%.
verdicts.explanation: Counting-from-the-sacrum itself separates the 802 records from 801 distinct subjects, counted with the same keying as the split. The handoff's '301 of 801 persons' and the ladder's 'all 801 readable' fit that. One remaining difference is that research directions calls the 802 'one per patient'.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry 802 records and 801 distinct subjects, each named by its unit. Whether two records share one person is the open point against research directions' 'one per patient'.

verdicts.topic: Calibrated renderer variance explained
verdicts.quote_a: the calibrated renderer about 90% of a held-out one
verdicts.quote_b: a per-frame smooth field reaches 93.9% against a 99.5% quantum-noise ceiling
verdicts.explanation: These are different quantities. About 90% is the calibrated renderer, with its device terms, after the log-compression correction. 93.9% adds a per-frame smooth field. Counting-levels carries both figures.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry both with their definitions. Note that the 93.9% predates the log-compression correction in counting-levels.

verdicts.topic: Licensing sentence and LSTV SOTA sentence copied from board to decisions
verdicts.quote_a: Published SOTA on radiographs is AUC 0.84, binary, single centre, at 62.3% prevalence.
verdicts.quote_b: At 4.0% that is population prevalence. Published SOTA is AUC 0.84, binary, single centre, at 62.3% prevalence.
verdicts.explanation: The decisions page repeats the board's text almost word for word: the SOTA sentence, the BUU 3,461/15/130 split, 465 grade-3 and 194 grade-4 slips, the 16 GB V100 against a 100 GB plan, the three replacement rules, and the clean-for-commercial list. It is one claim, not two confirmations.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry the shared text once, citing the board (2026-09-11) as its first appearance, with the Kwak 2025 source that research directions gives for the SOTA figure.

verdicts.topic: Method paragraph copied from counting-levels into the AIDaS proposal
verdicts.quote_a: Recall on real film: 99.14% per body for the film-trained detector; 71.67% for the same architecture trained on renders only.
verdicts.quote_b: A detector trained on real films reaches 99.14% per-body recall on real radiographs; the same architecture trained on renders only reaches 71.67%
verdicts.explanation: The AIDaS proposal (October) restates the counting-levels method and figures: 99.14%, 71.67%, the twelve arms, 93.9% and 99.5%. It is one source carried twice, and AIDaS changes the population-matched sacrum range to about 96–98%.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry these figures once, from counting-levels. Treat AIDaS as a copy, apart from its changed sacrum range (candidate 7) and its stale 80.9% (candidate 8).

verdicts.topic: Handoff and research-directions share the naming and transitional lines
verdicts.quote_a: 92 of 97 transitional validation and test persons sit in the current encoder's training lineage
verdicts.quote_b: 92 of 97 transitional validation and test persons sit in the v8 and v9 training splits
verdicts.explanation: The handoff and research directions are both dated 2026-10-08 and share lines: 97.4% and 74.8% naming, 92 of 97 transitional persons in the training lineage, and zero verified real-frame transitional persons against 35 needed. One claim from one catalog.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry each figure once, citing the handoff's results catalog as the source.

verdicts.topic: SyntheX and sim-to-real comparators repeated across four artifacts
verdicts.quote_a: Strong domain randomization — 6.44 mm with zero real training images against 6.46 for a real-trained control, on 366 real cadaveric C-arm images.
verdicts.quote_b: with landmark error 6.44 vs 6.46 mm and Dice 0.80 vs 0.79
verdicts.explanation: Ninety-three-pixels, the any-view plan and what-is-left all carry the same published SyntheX result: 6.44 against 6.46 mm, and CycleGAN 6.62 and ADDA 6.41. What-is-left names the source (Gao et al. 2023). It is one published claim repeated, not independent confirmation.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry it once, citing SyntheX (Gao et al. 2023) as what-is-left does.

verdicts.topic: Counting-from-the-sacrum and OR ledger share the C-ArmLSpine table
verdicts.quote_a: | Lateral, one vertebra in the field | | 72.85% | | 90.23% |
verdicts.quote_b: | 1 vertebra | | 72.8 | | — |
verdicts.explanation: Counting-from-the-sacrum and the OR ledger, both 2026-09-22, carry one C-ArmLSpine table, the ledger rounding 98.22/92.86/72.85/96.27/37.88 to one decimal. One discrepancy sits inside the shared table: the case count for the 98.2% figure, 141 in counting-from-the-sacrum against 148 in the ledger.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry the table once, superseded by the handoff's catalog values (97.4% and 74.8%, candidate 15). Resolve the 141 against 148 cases from the fold lists.

verdicts.topic: Per-region accuracy row copied from the ladder to the naming note
verdicts.quote_b: Per region at the tightest field, ours reads cervical 97.6%, thoracic 95.5%, lumbar 85.4%, sacrum 93.5%.
verdicts.explanation: The naming note (2026-09-18) carries the ladder's 96 px one-vertebra row (2026-09-13) region for region. The ladder's overall for that row is 96.9%, and the naming note gives 97.0% beside it.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry the row once, from the ladder, with its overall of 96.9% unless the result file gives 97.0% (candidate 46).

verdicts.topic: No published work uses DRRs to supply level identity to a 2D model
verdicts.quote_a: No published work uses DRRs to supply level identity to a 2D model; everyone uses them for landmarks, registration or 3D reconstruction.
verdicts.quote_b: No published work uses DRRs to supply level identity to a 2D model — everyone uses them for landmarks, registration or 3D reconstruction. This is the opening.
verdicts.explanation: The board (2026-09-11) and the decisions page both make the novelty claim in nearly the same words. Neither names a search, a date or a citation behind it.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry it only as an unverified novelty claim, until a dated literature search is recorded.

verdicts.topic: Published LSTV SOTA AUC 0.84 at 62.3% prevalence
verdicts.quote_a: Published SOTA on radiographs is AUC 0.84, binary, single centre, at 62.3% prevalence.
verdicts.quote_b: Kwak 2025 is the only 2-D LSTV model: accuracy 76.4 %, AUC 0.84 on 313 films at a 62 % positive rate
verdicts.explanation: The board and the decisions page give no paper for the figure. Research directions (2026-10-08) names its source, Kwak 2025, with 313 films, so the claim is sourced on one of the pages named. It gives 62% where the board gives 62.3%.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry AUC 0.84 at a 62% positive rate with the Kwak 2025 citation, from research directions.

verdicts.topic: CSXA is the largest annotated lateral set in existence
verdicts.quote_a: This is the largest annotated lateral set in existence and its absence is the single biggest gap in the corpus.
verdicts.quote_b: Buys: the largest annotated lateral spine dataset in existence, with physical scale per image.
verdicts.explanation: The field report says CSXA is the largest annotated lateral set in existence. The X-ray handoff (2026-09-03) repeats it with the count 4,963. Neither gives a comparison or a source.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry CSXA's size (4,963 films) and drop 'in existence', unless a survey of datasets is cited.

verdicts.topic: CM Spine is the only public intraoperative spine radiograph source
verdicts.quote_a: This is the only public intraoperative source, so no fluoroscopy is represented
verdicts.quote_b: Buys: the only public intraoperative spine radiographs — the one place surgical metal and labeled vertebrae coexist.
verdicts.explanation: The field report and the X-ray handoff (2026-09-03) both call CM Spine the only public intraoperative source, without a source. Later artifacts hold public C-arm sets, among them C-ArmLSpine, DeepFluoro and COBRA, so the claim no longer reads as true.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Drop 'only public intraoperative source'. Carry CM Spine as one of several public intraoperative or C-arm sets, per the OR ledger and the any-view plan.

verdicts.topic: Half of surveyed neurosurgeons report a wrong-level event
verdicts.quote_a: half of surveyed neurosurgeons report at least one wrong-level operation in their career
verdicts.quote_b: 50% of 415 surveyed surgeons had performed one, and 17% of 418 events led to legal action (Mody et al., Spine 2008).
verdicts.explanation: The naming note gives the figure without a citation, and counting-levels repeats it the same way. The AIDaS proposal sources it to Mody 2008 (50% of 415), and to Groff 2013 for almost 50% of 569 AANS/CNS respondents. So it is not unsourced on the pages named.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry it with AIDaS's citations: Mody 2008 (50% of 415 surgeons), or Groff 2013 for neurosurgeons.

verdicts.topic: Wrong-level incidence 1 in 830, registry of 34,544, 81% of surgeons
verdicts.quote_a: Wrong-level spine surgery is 1 in 830 operations in a 34,544-case registry (1 in 240 in the thoracic spine), and half of surveyed spine surgeons have done it once; 81% of events are a count that went wrong under fluoroscopy.
verdicts.quote_b: In a registry of 34,544 degenerative spine operations at 27 hospitals (2012–2022) the incidence was 0.12% (95% CI 0.09–0.16) ... Intraoperative disorientation was the cause in 81.3% (Furuya et al., Bone Joint J 2026).
verdicts.explanation: Counting-levels cites no source on the page; it only links to a one-page version 'with every source'. AIDaS sources the same registry to Furuya 2026, and 0.12% is the same as 1 in 830. AIDaS's 81.3% is 'intraoperative disorientation', which counting-levels restates more strongly as 'a count that went wrong under fluoroscopy'.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry 0.12% (95% CI 0.09–0.16) and 81.3% intraoperative disorientation with the Furuya 2026 citation, from AIDaS, in its wording.

verdicts.topic: Surgeon unassisted vs assisted localisation 69.6% / 97.6%
verdicts.quote_a: Surgeon and CT-registration comparators are published literature.
verdicts.quote_b: Manbachi 2018 is the human naming number on hard intraoperative films, 69.6 % unassisted and 97.6 % assisted.
verdicts.explanation: The naming note attributes 69.6% and 97.6% only to 'published literature'. Research directions (2026-10-08) names the source, Manbachi 2018, with the same values.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry 69.6% unassisted and 97.6% assisted with the Manbachi 2018 citation, from research directions.

verdicts.topic: A 28-point sim-to-real tax matches what the field reports
verdicts.quote_a: A detector trained on 6,650 renders and no real image gets 71.7% on real radiographs against 99.1% for the same architecture trained on real film — and that 28-point sim-to-real tax matches what the field reports elsewhere almost exactly.
verdicts.quote_b: Also withdrawn: the planned Pelphix citation. Its 99.2→71.7 is surgical-phase accuracy, not detection. The 0.03-point agreement was a coincidence between two different quantities and would not have survived review.
verdicts.explanation: The claim is not shared: ninety-three-pixels (2026-09-21) does not carry it but contradicts it. It withdrew the only matching citation and says 'Your 71.67% has no peer'. Counting-from-the-sacrum, a day later, makes the claim again with no paper.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Drop 'matches what the field reports'. Carry ninety-three-pixels' statement that 71.67% has no published peer.

verdicts.topic: Sixth lumbar vertebra prevalence about 2% / L5 lowest 97% of the time
verdicts.quote_a: A sixth lumbar vertebra occurs in roughly 2% of people, so the model is rewarded for never predicting one.
verdicts.quote_b: About 22 of 802 cases carry an L6 at all, roughly 2.7%.
verdicts.explanation: The two-anchors page states a population prior with no source. The decisions page gives a count within the CTSpinoPelvic1K cohort, which is its own basis. These are not the same claim, and research directions later gives v11 as 18 L6 by label.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry the cohort count with its version (v11: 18 by label, 16 by readers, per research directions). Cite a source for any population prevalence or drop it.

verdicts.topic: Counting from C2 is the only definitive method
verdicts.quote_a: counting from C2 on whole‑spine imaging is the only definitive method
verdicts.quote_b: This is the documented failure mode, and it is a property of the target , not the backbone.
verdicts.explanation: The two-anchors page's 'documented failure mode' is a model always calling the lowest lumbar vertebra L5. It is not the rib audit's premise about counting from C2. The rib audit's statement is unsourced, but the second page does not repeat it.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Treat as two separate unsourced statements, each needing its own citation.

verdicts.topic: Lateral naming at any device is already at the ceiling
verdicts.quote_a: Lateral naming at any device is already at the ceiling.
verdicts.quote_b: the comparator 97.6 % cannot be exceeded at any reachable n
verdicts.explanation: The any-view plan's line marks itself 'Inferred from the record', based on 96.4% zero-shot against 97.4% fine-tuned. The handoff's line is a statistical-power statement about paper 2's LevelCheck comparator. Different claims, not one shared one.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry the any-view statement as an inference from zero-shot 96.4% against fine-tuned 97.4%, and the handoff's as a power limit on paper 2.

verdicts.topic: ResNet50 identifies the source dataset at 86.6% F1
verdicts.quote_a: A ResNet50 identifies source dataset from chest X-ray contours alone at 86.6% F1 — the signature survives intensity normalisation.
verdicts.quote_b: A ResNet50 identifies source dataset from chest X-ray contours alone at 86.6% F1
verdicts.explanation: The decisions page gives this finding about chest X-rays as evidence for its architecture, with no citation or run behind it. No other artifact in the set carries it.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry it only with a citation for the chest X-ray dataset-identification study, otherwise drop it.

verdicts.topic: Wrong-level cost 52 minutes and 183 mGy
verdicts.quote_a: One quaternary centre performed 179 preoperative percutaneous gold-fiducial placements over 38 months, 176 of them thoracic , at a mean of 52 minutes and 183 mGy each
verdicts.quote_b: one centre placed 179 preoperative gold fiducials over 38 months, 176 thoracic, at a mean of 51.9 min and 183 mGy each (Siminski et al., AJNR 2023)
verdicts.explanation: The naming note gives the figures without a source. The AIDaS proposal gives the same series with its citation, Siminski 2023, and the unrounded 51.9 minutes.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry 179 placements, 51.9 min and 183 mGy with the Siminski 2023 citation, from AIDaS.

verdicts.topic: Cadaver work needs no IRB
verdicts.quote_a: cadaver work is not human-subjects research and needs no IRB, only the program's and biosafety approval.
verdicts.quote_b: (c) Cadaver validation through the Body Bequest Program (a research proposal to the program and to biosafety; not human-subjects research under the Common Rule).
verdicts.explanation: Counting-levels and the AIDaS proposal both say cadaver work is not human-subjects research and needs only the program's and biosafety approval. Neither cites a regulation text or an institutional determination. AIDaS's determination 2026_269 covers only public de-identified data, so it does not source this claim.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry it only with an institutional determination or a written statement from the program confirming that no IRB review is needed for the cadaver study.

verdicts.topic: Field report status lines
verdicts.quote_a: Level head — not started. The spec is explicit that detection must be stable first, and it is only now stable.
verdicts.quote_b: single-vertebra ResNets on 96 px targets with a marker channel; BiGRU run labeller per model and rung; flip TTA; entropy for the queue
verdicts.explanation: The field report predates the X-ray handoff of 2026-09-03 and says the level head is not started, BUU is 77 files and CSXA is not obtained. By 2026-09-14 the FluoroCap map has a 4-model level ensemble with a BiGRU and self-training. The board (2026-09-11) has the CSXA converter validated on 4,963 films, and decisions lists 7,204 BUU. The flip TTA at inference does not contradict the report's training flip being disabled.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry the later state: the level models exist (FluoroCap map, 2026-09-14; handoff, 2026-10-08), CSXA and full BUU are held. Mark the field report's status lines as of its date.

verdicts.topic: Board asks the owner to purge IRB files; decisions records it done
verdicts.quote_a: Purging needs a history rewrite and a force-push — say go and it is done in ten minutes.
verdicts.quote_b: Removed from every ref with git-filter-repo , both remotes force-pushed, verified zero commits/trees/blobs remaining.
verdicts.explanation: On 2026-09-11 the board waits on the owner's go to purge the IRB files. The decisions page, which follows it, records the purge as done and verified. Only the request to GitHub support to purge cached views of the old SHAs remains open.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry the purge as done (decisions), with the GitHub cache-purge request still the owner's to do.

verdicts.topic: Running jobs and pending audits dated 2026-09-13 to 2026-09-22
verdicts.quote_a: Whether a release id is a person. CTSpinoPelvic1K is built from CT colonography, which scans each patient both prone and supine. ... An audit is running; it is not assumed to be fine.
verdicts.quote_b: A cross-validation over all 376 transitional patients is running

Research directions (2026-10-08) states CTSpinoPelvic1K is one record per patient, which settles the audit, and reports results on 376 held-out renders. The handoff (2026-10-08) says nothing after 2026-09-27 changed the banks or models, so these are no longer current. No later page reports the fleet detector's result.

verdicts.quote_a: The census job is built (PR #76) and goes to the grid next. ... The census (PR #76, run on 2026-10-22: 140 groups, 7,008,826 files, 7.3 TB; docs/research/data-manifest/MANIFEST.md)

verdicts.topic: AIDaS proposal placeholders and the rib audit's unpushed v5
verdicts.quote_a: Learned refiners and Fourier low-band swaps are being measured as arms; results are pending.
verdicts.quote_b: v5 exists as a local tree on the grid at data/v5_final . Nothing has been pushed to a HuggingFace branch.
verdicts.explanation: AIDaS (October 2026, due 16 October) calls the refiner and low-band-swap arms pending. Yet counting-levels (September 2026) already reports them: about ten points for the swap, about eight for the refiners, with every effect inside the 26-point seed spread. So AIDaS was behind when written, but no source later than AIDaS shows its state. The rib audit's unpushed v5 has no later source either.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry the arm results from counting-levels. A record of the AIDaS submission, and of a v5 push to the HuggingFace branch, would settle whether the two statements still hold.

canonical_check.why: The decisions artifact carries the board's decisions, corpus table and licensing sentences forward verbatim and closes the board's open action: the board asks the owner to say go on the IRB-file purge, the decisions artifact records the purge done with git-filter-repo and verified. The decisions artifact also moves numbers the board gives (retraining target ~13,500 to ~34,000, Spinal-AI2024 from do-not-download to revisit), which is what superseding looks like, though the board is dated 2026-09-11 and the decisions artifact is undated.

clusters.unsourced_summary: The cluster asserts a set of field-level claims with no paper, run id or search behind them, and several are copied between artifacts. The board and decisions artifacts both state that no published work uses DRRs to supply level identity to a 2D model and that the published LSTV state of the art is AUC 0.84 at 62.3% prevalence; only research-directions later names the second as Kwak 2025. The field report and the X-ray data handoff both call CSXA the largest annotated lateral set in existence and CM Spine the only public intraoperative source, while other artifacts treat DeepFluoro and C-ArmLSpine as real intraoperative sources. Counting-from-the-sacrum says published class-agnostic C-arm detection reaches 0.96-0.98 and that a 28-point sim-to-real tax matches the field, while ninety-three-pixels says no per-vertebra recall on real fluoroscopy is published and the 71.67% has no peer. The naming note and counting-levels repeat that half of surveyed neurosurgeons report a wrong-level event, 69.6%/97.6% surgeon accuracies, 52 minutes and 183 mGy per event, and 1 in 830 incidence; only the AIDaS proposal and research-directions attach names (Mody 2008, Manbachi 2018, Siminski 2023, Furuya 2026). Counting-against-two-anchors gives a 2% sixth-lumbar prior and a 'documented failure mode' with no document, and the rib audit calls counting from C2 the only definitive method. The decisions artifact gives a ResNet50 source-dataset F1 of 86.6% with no record. The any-view plan's 'lateral naming is at the ceiling' is graded Inferred with no second real device measured, and counting-levels asserts cadaver work needs no IRB while the proposal says the determination covers public de-identified data only.
clusters.stale_summary: The field report (undated, earliest) says the level head is not started, the ignore mask is unused, BUU holds 77 files and CSXA is blocked; the X-ray data handoff's grid state is 'verified 3 Sep 2026' with 800 BUU images never ingested and 0 CSXA on disk. The board (2026-09-11) waits on the owner for the IRB-file purge and is normalising ~22,000 radiographs; the decisions artifact records the purge done, lists Spinal-AI2024 as 'revisit' and a GitHub support ticket open. The ladder (2026-09-13) has jobs 40215523/40215525 running and the VinDr lumbar pipeline in progress; the naming note (2026-09-18) has the 376-patient transitional CV and the Klinwichit training running; counting-from-the-sacrum (2026-09-22) has an A/B and the id-is-a-person audit running and a fleet detector training; the OR ledger (2026-09-22) lists several jobs running, a re-score pending and no device fitted beyond the Cios Fusion; ninety-three-pixels (2026-09-21) has 8 GPU jobs and a decision on the table; what-is-left says the band test is 'being measured right now'. The handoff (2026-10-08) records the disclosure submitted 2026-09-25 with the provisional not recorded, the CNS talk 31 Oct-4 Nov, the Ceph migration and dataset letters not sent; research-directions (2026-10-08) says nothing ran on the grid and letters are not sent. The any-view plan (2026-10-21) has the census job built (PR #76) and going to the grid next, IPCAI 2025 'not yet', and is marked confidential before the provisional and 'before the talk'. The AIDaS proposal (due 2026-10-16, now past) carries [to confirm] placeholders, pending refiner and Fourier arms and a $20,000 request for 2027. The rib audit's v5 is a local tree with nothing pushed and sacral tests next; the two-anchors arms are proposed and not run; the pipeline map's versions are as of its 2026-09-14 commit.
clusters.notes: All 18 records were read whole and every quantity listed was checked against the plain text under /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/1b2f17bd-1fd4-5865-b98a-4797cc8ea3ad/scratchpad/text/SchwingNet/. The cluster spans five detector generations (958 images, 4,327, 11,007, 12,709 films, and render-only arms) and several C-ArmLSpine runs (120/141/148/149 cases), and most numeric disagreements are different runs reported as one fact rather than errors; the task was to list them, not to settle them. Items flagged with a caveat: the Ljubljana entries may be two distinct sets; the two patch sizes may belong to two networks; 90% vs 93.9% variance explained may be two quantities. The handoff's 'VinDr-SpineXR (0 of 10,466)' means not in the level bank, not a holding count, and its '2,293 DeepFluoro vendor frames' are the unused vendor frames, distinct from the 366. A file fluorocap-reality-check-czudvb.txt appeared in a grep but is not a member of this cluster and was not used. No e-mail, phone or address was reproduced; people are named by role (the owner, the radiologist, readers).

clusters.cluster: Renders, physics and the sim-to-real gap

candidates.topic: Whether a registered real frame beats its DRR twin as training data (Rapuri 2026 Table 1, DeepFluoro landmarks)
candidates.statement_a: Training on the real frame beats training on its DRR twin: 4.89 vs 7.83 mm; so build the registration route, keep the DRR only as augmentation and fine-tune on real frames.
candidates.quote_a: The DRR at the registered pose is a by-product you get for free, but training on the real frame beats training on that DRR (4.89 vs 7.83 mm landmarks on DeepFluoro, Rapuri 2026 ).
candidates.statement_b: In the same table, DRRs with +/-2.5 degree view augmentation were the best arm at every threshold (4.87 / 6.02 / 9.73), beating real-frame training (4.89) and the generator; physics plus pose augmentation wins everywhere.
candidates.quote_b: DRRs with ±2.5° view augmentation were the best arm at every threshold ( 4.87 / 6.02 / 9.73 ). A generator wins where the detector is already confident and loses where it is not; physics plus pose augmentation wins everywhere.
candidates.why_it_matters: The cluster's answer that registered real frames beat their DRR twins rests on the unaugmented DRR arm only; a planner reading lift-before-label would spend the budget on registering real frames, while what-is-left's reading of the same table says pose-augmented physics DRRs already match or beat them.

candidates.topic: Fraction of a real DeepFluoro frame's variance explained by physics alone (and by the calibrated renderer held out)
candidates.statement_a: Physics alone explains 80.9% of a real frame's attenuation variance (NCC 0.899); a per-frame surface takes the calibrated model to 93.9%.
candidates.quote_a: 80.9% of a real frame's attenuation variance (NCC 0.899), same band shape in every specimen
candidates.statement_b: The stored frames are log-compressed display images; read correctly, physics alone explains 86% rather than 80%, and the calibrated renderer about 90% of a held-out frame.
candidates.quote_b: The stored DeepFluoro frames also turned out to be log-compressed display images; read correctly, physics alone explains 86% of a real frame rather than 80%, and the calibrated renderer about 90% of a held-out one.
candidates.why_it_matters: The 80.9% figure was measured on a mis-read intensity scale; a planner budgeting what a learned term could add would start from the wrong gap (19 points instead of 14) and from an in-sample 93.9% rather than a held-out ~90%.

candidates.topic: Physics-only variance explained and the smooth-field figure quoted in the October proposal and the IRB draft
candidates.statement_a: The renderer explains 80.9% of a real frame's variance, nine device terms add 4.3 points, a per-frame smooth field reaches 93.9% against a 99.5% ceiling (also in the Retrospective Fluoroscopy Protocol).
candidates.quote_a: our renderer explains 80.9% of a real frame's variance; nine calibrated device terms add 4.3 points, held out by specimen; a per-frame smooth field reaches 93.9% against a 99.5% quantum-noise ceiling
candidates.statement_b: Read correctly, physics alone explains 86% and the calibrated renderer about 90% of a held-out frame.
candidates.quote_b: read correctly, physics alone explains 86% of a real frame rather than 80%, and the calibrated renderer about 90% of a held-out one.
candidates.why_it_matters: The grant proposal (October 2026) and the IRB draft carry the pre-correction numbers even though the correction is dated to the 21 September runs; a reviewer or planner would quote 80.9 / 93.9 as current.

candidates.topic: What remains at bone scale after physics and the per-frame field: 'nothing local' versus 2 to 7 times the noise floor
candidates.statement_a: After geometry, physics and nine device terms the residual is a smooth per-frame field with nothing local in it (0.4% of variance at 2 px or finer), so there is nothing for a regional network to learn.
candidates.quote_a: what is left is a smooth per-frame field with nothing local in it — 0.4% of variance at ≤2 px — so there is nothing for a regional network to learn.
candidates.statement_b: After the field the 2 to 16 px bands sit at 0.1 to 0.8% of variance each, two to seven times the noise floor; the 'nothing local' claim was too strong.
candidates.quote_b: After the field, the 2–16 px bands sit at 0.1–0.8% of the frame's variance each — two to seven times the noise floor, not at it.
candidates.why_it_matters: This is the claim the clustering's supersession rests on: ninety-three closes the door on any local learned term, what-is-left reopens it narrowly (bone-edge sharpness) while still advising against a generator.

candidates.topic: What the residual after the calibrated render consists of
candidates.statement_a: The residual edge lines are the real frame being sharper than a 1 mm CT can render, plus bowel gas that moved; the dark right half is collimation and vignette absorbed by the smooth field.
candidates.quote_a: The edge lines are the real frame being sharper than the render: the CT is 1 mm voxels magnified 1.5× onto 0.19 mm pixels, and a render cannot hold detail the CT never had. The bowel mottle is gas that moved between the CT and the fluoroscopy.
candidates.statement_b: Measured by region with the collimator border kept separate, the border ring (a fifth of the field) holds about two thirds of the residual; inside it cortical edges agree to within a few grey levels at every bone thickness; an earlier thin-bone deficit was the border counted as bone and is withdrawn.
candidates.quote_b: the border ring, a fifth of the field, holds about two thirds of the residual, because the real frame falls off through the penumbra and the render stops at a hard edge; inside it, cortical edges agree with the real frame to within a few grey levels at every bone thickness. A thin-bone deficit reported earlier was that border counted as a bone edge, and it has been withdrawn.
candidates.why_it_matters: A planner reading what-is-left would try to add sub-CT sharpness; reading counting-levels would fix the penumbra model at the collimator edge instead. The two pages name different things as the dominant residual.

candidates.topic: Sacrum recall on real DeepFluoro frames of a detector trained only on renders of DeepFluoro's own CTs (population-matched, leave-one-specimen-out)
candidates.statement_a: 90 to 97% of real frames, six specimens held out in turn.
candidates.quote_a: A detector trained on renders of DeepFluoro's own CTs finds the sacrum on 90–97% of the real frames, six specimens held out in turn.
candidates.statement_b: About 96 to 98% of real frames, leave-one-specimen-out (same wording in the Retrospective Fluoroscopy Protocol).
candidates.quote_b: A detector trained only on calibrated renders of DeepFluoro's own CTs finds the sacrum on about 96–98% of real frames (leave-one-specimen-out).
candidates.why_it_matters: The population-matched arm is the ceiling the whole argument 'the population, not the renderer, limits it' hangs on; the proposal quotes a tighter, higher range than the run report it draws from.

candidates.topic: The population-matched DeepFluoro sacrum number after the init-exposure audit
candidates.statement_a: The 100% DeepFluoro sacrum number is ruled not the manuscript's method (render init saw 44.8% of the test specimen's poses, device terms fitted on its pixels); the clean render-only number for specimen 18-1109 is 88.5 to 91.3% at conf 0.05 over three seeds.
candidates.quote_a: The clean render-only number for that specimen is 88.5–91.3% at conf 0.05 (three seeds).
candidates.statement_b: A detector trained only on calibrated renders of that dataset's own CTs finds the sacrum on about 96 to 98% of real frames.
candidates.quote_b: a detector trained only on calibrated renders of that dataset's own CTs finds the sacrum on about 96–98% of real frames, but trained on renders of other living whole-body CTs it finds it on about 64–77%
candidates.why_it_matters: The ledger (22 Sep) found the high same-device numbers contaminated by init exposure and gives 88.5 to 91.3% as clean; the later IRB draft and grant still quote 96 to 98%.

candidates.topic: The render-trained two-class detector's pooled sacrum recall on real DeepFluoro frames (76.9%)
candidates.statement_a: Trained on 597 calibrated synthetic frames, finds the sacrum on 76.9% of 365 real frames (by specimen 47.8 to 96.2%).
candidates.quote_a: finds the sacrum on 76.9% of 365 real frames pooled over all six specimens (by specimen 47.8–96.2%)
candidates.statement_b: The 76.9% belongs to the anchor_none_r2 generation; the v2 generation every real fine-tune started from pools to 64.0%, and render-only v2 on 18-1109 is 55.6%.
candidates.quote_b: The manuscript's 76.9% belongs to the anchor_none_r2 generation; the v2 generation every real fine-tune started from pools to 64.0%.
candidates.why_it_matters: What-is-left, counting-levels and the grant reason from 76.9% (or the 64/77 pair); a planner must know which generation of renders and which detector the number belongs to before comparing arms.

candidates.topic: Held-out gain of the nine calibrated device terms on the DeepFluoro Cios Fusion
candidates.statement_a: Nine device terms add +4.3 points with scatter boxed (median held-out +4.1, range -3.1 to +8.0).
candidates.quote_a: Scatter width boxed to 6–16 px: +4.3 , 15.8 px with spread 0.4, every term stable — the calibration now applied.
candidates.statement_b: The Cios Fusion device card lists held-out R-squared physics to fitted as 0.899 to 0.905, a gain of +1.3.
candidates.why_it_matters: The same nine terms on the same 366 pairs are credited with +4.3 points in one page and +1.3 in the device-card fit that the ledger says reproduces the shipped folds to 1e-3 per term; a planner pricing device calibration against randomisation needs to know which is the held-out gain.

candidates.topic: Whether physics-styled synthetic frames are calibrated to the real device
candidates.statement_a: The CT-to-fluoro map was calibrated, not learned, and transfers because every fitted term belongs to the device.
candidates.quote_a: So it was calibrated , not learned, and it transfers to whole-spine CTs because every fitted term belongs to
candidates.statement_b: Physics-styled frames are not yet statistically inside the real domain (NPS distance 0.111 against a real-vs-real floor of 0.015), so that claim is not made.
candidates.quote_b: Real-vs-styled distances on the Cios card: NPS 0.111 against a real-vs-real floor of 0.015; grey histogram 3.1 vs 0.14
candidates.why_it_matters: 'Calibrated' in ninety-three means variance explained per frame; the ledger measures the styled corpus as a distribution and finds it outside the real domain, which is what a detector trains on.

candidates.topic: Whether the project's renderer is already at the DeepDRR/SyntheX level
candidates.statement_a: The renderer is already at the DeepDRR/SyntheX level; only its randomisation list needs checking.
candidates.quote_a: strong domain randomisation on 10,000 DRRs from 20 CTs beat training on the 366 real frames (5.95 vs 6.46 mm) and CycleGAN or ADDA added nothing on top (SyntheX). Your renderer is already here
candidates.statement_b: A saturating clip on 8 to 11 correlated terms meant the device-card renders reached only 1.7 to 5.1% of the fitted joint distribution, with 94.9 to 98.3% of frames carrying a pinned term; the replacement sampler is not adopted.
candidates.quote_b: A clip meant to stop implausible draws was applied to 8–11 correlated terms at once, and it saturates rather than truncates
candidates.why_it_matters: Lift's recommendation to skip renderer work and move to registration assumes the renderer is sound; a week later the sampler was found to pin almost every frame.

candidates.topic: Detection on C-ArmLSpine from renders alone (device never seen, no real frames)
candidates.statement_a: Detection from renders alone is 0.3%; detection does not transfer from today's renders.
candidates.quote_a: | Detection from renders alone | | 0.3% | | Detection does not transfer from today's renders. |
candidates.statement_b: The render-only detector on C-ArmLSpine whole frames finds 73.2% of sacra and 17.1% of vertebrae (body boxes), 31.7% under outline truth and 54.7% under the centre rule.
candidates.quote_b: The render-only detector reads 31.7% outline / 54.7% centre.
candidates.why_it_matters: Whether renders carry anything to a new device decides whether the physics-renderer ablation (#69) is worth running; 0.3% says nothing transfers, the ledger's conventions say a third to a half of vertebrae do.

candidates.topic: Detection on C-ArmLSpine with the device held out but other devices' real frames in training
candidates.statement_a: Sacrum found 83.9% and vertebra recall 90.6% on whole frames once truth boxes share one convention (also 90.6% in Counting From The Sacrum).
candidates.quote_a: sacrum found 83.9%, vertebra recall 90.6% on whole frames once truth boxes use one convention
candidates.statement_b: Detection with other devices' real frames plus renders is 80.5%, and 84.0% once 24 frames of the device are added.
candidates.quote_b: | Detection with other devices' real frames plus renders | | 80.5% | | Real frames from any device carry most of it. |
candidates.why_it_matters: The baseline for a never-seen C-arm is given as 90.6% (September) and 80.5% (October) without saying what changed; the gap is the margin a planner would attribute to adding device frames.

candidates.topic: Exact lateral level naming on C-ArmLSpine with the device in training
candidates.statement_a: 98.22% exact on lateral whole frames (141 cases, 617 vertebrae, 5-fold CV); the ledger gives 98.2% over 148 cases.

verdicts.topic: Whether a registered real frame beats its DRR twin as training data (Rapuri 2026 Table 1, DeepFluoro landmarks)

Lift Before Label (15 Sep 2026) compares only the unaugmented DRR twin with the real frame; What Is Left adds a third arm, DRRs with ±2.5° view augmentation at 4.87. The numbers do not conflict; the pages compare different arms.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry all three arms from What Is Left's reading of Table 1: real 4.89, unaugmented DRR 7.83, pose-augmented DRR 4.87 (6.02 / 9.73 at the other thresholds). Qualify Lift Before Label's 'real beats DRR' as true only against the unaugmented DRR.

Counting Levels Under Fluoroscopy (September 2026) uses the leave-one-specimen-out runs of 21 September and revises that figure in its own words: once the frames are read as log-compressed display images, physics alone explains 86% 'rather than 80%'. Its 'about 90% of a held-out one' is for the calibrated renderer on a held-out frame, which is not the same quantity as Ninety-Three's 93.9% with a per-frame surface.
